וְעֵ֤ין נֹאֵ֨ף ׀ שָׁ֤מְרָֽה נֶ֣שֶׁף לֵ֭אמֹר לֹא־תְשׁוּרֵ֣נִי עָ֑יִן וְסֵ֖תֶר פָּנִ֣ים יָשִֽׂים׃
In the dark they break into houses;[^17] by day they shut themselves in; they do not know the light.
חָתַ֥ר בַּחֹ֗שֶׁךְ בָּ֫תִּ֥ים יוֹמָ֥ם חִתְּמוּ־לָ֗מוֹ לֹא־יָ֥דְּעוּ אֽוֹר׃
For to all of them the morning is deep darkness,[^18] for they are well acquainted with the terrors of deep darkness.[^19]
כִּ֤י יַחְדָּ֨ו ׀ בֹּ֣קֶר לָ֣מוֹ צַלְמָ֑וֶת כִּֽי־יַ֝כִּ֗יר בַּלְה֥וֹת צַלְמָֽוֶת׃
He is swift on the surface of the waters;[^20] their portion in the land is cursed; he does not turn toward the vineyards.[^21]
קַֽל־ה֤וּא ׀ עַל־פְּנֵי־מַ֗יִם תְּקֻלַּ֣ל חֶלְקָתָ֣ם בָּאָ֑רֶץ לֹֽא־יִ֝פְנֶה דֶּ֣רֶךְ כְּרָמִֽים׃
Drought and heat snatch away the snow waters; so does Sheol[^22] those who have sinned.
צִיָּ֤ה גַם־חֹ֗ם יִגְזְל֥וּ מֵֽימֵי־שֶׁ֗לֶג שְׁא֣וֹל חָטָֽאוּ׃
The womb forgets him; the worm feeds on him with relish;[^23] he is remembered no more, and wickedness is broken like a tree.
יִשְׁכָּ֘חֵ֤הוּ רֶ֨חֶם ׀ מְתָ֘ק֤וֹ רִמָּ֗ה ע֥וֹד לֹֽא־יִזָּכֵ֑ר וַתִּשָּׁבֵ֖ר כָּעֵ֣ץ עַוְלָֽה׃
He feeds on[^24] the barren woman who bears no child, and does no good to the widow.
רֹעֵ֣[t]ה עֲ֭קָרָה לֹ֣א תֵלֵ֑ד וְ֝אַלְמָנָ֗ה לֹ֣א יְיֵטִֽיב׃
Yet by his power he prolongs the life of the mighty;[^25] they rise up when they had no hope of living.[^26]
וּמָשַׁ֣ךְ אַבִּירִ֣ים בְּכֹח֑וֹ יָ֝ק֗וּם וְֽלֹא־יַאֲמִ֥ין בַּֽחַיִּֽין׃
He lets them rest secure,[^27] and they are supported, and his eyes are on their ways.
יִתֶּן־ל֣וֹ לָ֭בֶטַח וְיִשָּׁעֵ֑ן וְ֝עֵינֵ֗יהוּ עַל־דַּרְכֵיהֶֽם׃
They are exalted for a little while, and then they are gone. They are brought low and gathered up like everyone else;[^28] they are cut off like the heads of grain.
ר֤וֹמּוּ מְּעַ֨ט ׀ וְֽאֵינֶ֗נּוּ וְֽהֻמְּכ֗וּ כַּכֹּ֥ל יִקָּפְצ֑וּן וּכְרֹ֖אשׁ שִׁבֹּ֣לֶת יִמָּֽלוּ׃
If it is not so, who can prove me a liar and reduce my words to nothing?"
וְאִם־לֹ֣א אֵ֭פוֹ מִ֣י יַכְזִיבֵ֑נִי וְיָשֵׂ֥ם לְ֝אַ֗ל מִלָּתִֽי׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain. The *times* are probably times of judgment, when God would call the wicked to account.
n.2: The Hebrew text is written "and they know" but read "and those who know him".
n.3: That is, the days when he judges.
n.4: Literally "They move boundaries". The subject is not stated; the wicked are meant. Boundary stones marked a family's land (Deuteronomy 19:14).
n.5: A pledge was something taken as security for a debt (compare Deuteronomy 24:17).
n.6: Literally "seeking early for prey". From here to verse 8, *they* are the poor of verse 4.
n.7: The Hebrew of this line is uncertain. Literally "the desert, to him, bread for the young ones".
n.8: Hebrew *belilo*, "his fodder", perhaps the wicked man's. Some scholars divide the word as *beli lo*, "not his": "they reap in a field that is not theirs".
n.9: Literally "They snatch the orphan from the breast": the wicked, as in verses 2–4.
n.10: Literally "and against the poor they take pledges".
n.11: Hebrew *shurot*, "walls" or "rows": perhaps the terrace walls of olive groves, or rows of olive trees.
n.12: Or "the dying groan": the same Hebrew consonants read with different vowels.
n.13: Literally "the soul of the wounded".
n.14: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job.
n.15: Hebrew *tiflah*, "what is unfitting", the word in 1:22. The same consonants can be read *tefillah*, "prayer": "yet God does not heed their prayer".
n.16: Literally "at the light". Some take it to mean "before the light" or "at dusk". Some scholars read *lo or*, "when there is no light", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.17: Literally "he digs through houses", through their walls of mud brick.
n.18: Hebrew *tsalmavet*, "deep darkness", traditionally read as "the shadow of death". Also later in the verse.
n.19: Literally "for he recognizes the terrors of deep darkness".
n.20: Verses 18–24 describe the swift end of the wicked, as the friends do (compare 18:5–21 and 20:4–29), though Job has just said that God does not call them to account (verses 1 and 12; 21:7–34). Interpreters explain this in different ways: Job is quoting the friends' view in order to reject it (verse 25), or wishing it were true ("Let him be swift …"), or these verses belong to a speech of Bildad or Zophar in this third round of speeches (see the note at 25:1). The Hebrew has no marker, and they are translated here as they stand, as part of Job's speech. The picture in this line is of the wicked man swept away like foam on the water.
n.21: Literally "he does not turn the way of the vineyards": he will not go out to enjoy them.
n.22: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.24: Literally "He grazes on", that is, he devours what she has.
n.25: Literally "he draws out the mighty by his power". *He* is probably God, as in verse 23, though the Hebrew does not say. Or "he drags away the mighty by his power", of the wicked man.
n.26: Literally "he rises and does not believe in life".
n.28: Literally "like all". The Greek Septuagint reads "like mallow (in the heat)", a plant that wilts quickly.

v: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered:[^1]
וַ֭יַּעַן בִּלְדַּ֥ד הַשֻּׁחִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"Dominion and dread are his; he makes peace in his high places.[^2]
הַמְשֵׁ֣ל וָפַ֣חַד עִמּ֑וֹ עֹשֶׂ֥ה שָׁ֝ל֗וֹם בִּמְרוֹמָֽיו׃
Can his troops be counted?[^3] On whom does his light not rise?
הֲיֵ֣שׁ מִ֭סְפָּר לִגְדוּדָ֑יו וְעַל־מִ֝֗י לֹא־יָק֥וּם אוֹרֵֽהוּ׃
How then can a mortal be in the right before God? How can one born of a woman be pure?[^4]
וּמַה־יִּצְדַּ֣ק אֱנ֣וֹשׁ עִם־אֵ֑ל וּמַה־יִּ֝זְכֶּ֗ה יְל֣וּד אִשָּֽׁה׃
Look, even the moon is not bright,[^5] and the stars are not pure in his eyes;
הֵ֣ן עַד־יָ֭רֵחַ וְלֹ֣א יַאֲהִ֑יל וְ֝כוֹכָבִ֗ים לֹא־זַכּ֥וּ בְעֵינָֽיו׃
how much less a mortal, who is a maggot, and a human being,[^6] who is a worm!"
אַ֭ף כִּֽי־אֱנ֣וֹשׁ רִמָּ֑ה וּבֶן־אָ֝דָ֗ם תּוֹלֵעָֽה׃ פ

n.1: Bildad's third speech is very short, and Zophar, who spoke after Bildad in the first two rounds of speeches (chapters 11 and 20), has no third speech. Many interpreters think that parts of chapters 24–27 have been moved from their original speakers: some, for example, give 26:5–14 to Bildad and 27:13–23 to Zophar. The text is translated here as it stands.
n.2: Literally "Ruling and dread are with him". *His high places* are the heavens.
n.3: Literally "Is there a number to his troops?": probably the stars, or the heavenly beings who serve him.
n.4: Compare Eliphaz's words in 4:17–19 and 15:14–16.
n.5: Literally "Look, as far as the moon, and it does not shine". Hebrew *ya'ahil*, a verb found only here, probably "shine".
n.6: Literally "a son of *adam*", that is, of humankind.

v: Then Job answered:
וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"How you have helped the powerless![^1] How you have saved the arm that has no strength!
מֶה־עָזַ֥רְתָּ לְלֹא־כֹ֑חַ ה֝וֹשַׁ֗עְתָּ זְר֣וֹעַ לֹא־עֹֽז׃
How you have counseled one who has no wisdom, and what a wealth of sound wisdom[^2] you have made known!
מַה־יָּ֭עַצְתָּ לְלֹ֣א חָכְמָ֑ה וְ֝תוּשִׁיָּ֗ה לָרֹ֥ב הוֹדָֽעְתָּ׃
With whose help have you uttered these words?[^3] Whose breath[^4] has come out of you?
אֶת־מִ֭י הִגַּ֣דְתָּ מִלִּ֑ין וְנִשְׁמַת־מִ֝י יָצְאָ֥ה מִמֶּֽךָּ׃
The shades of the dead[^5] writhe beneath the waters, and so do those who live in them.
הָרְפָאִ֥ים יְחוֹלָ֑לוּ מִתַּ֥חַת מַ֝֗יִם וְשֹׁכְנֵיהֶֽם׃
Sheol[^6] is naked before him, and Abaddon[^7] has no covering.
עָר֣וֹם שְׁא֣וֹל נֶגְדּ֑וֹ וְאֵ֥ין כְּ֝ס֗וּת לָֽאֲבַדּֽוֹן׃
He stretches out the north over empty space[^8] and hangs the earth on nothing.
נֹטֶ֣ה צָפ֣וֹן עַל־תֹּ֑הוּ תֹּ֥לֶה אֶ֝֗רֶץ עַל־בְּלִי־מָֽה׃
He wraps up the waters in his clouds, and the cloud does not burst under them.
צֹרֵֽר־מַ֥יִם בְּעָבָ֑יו וְלֹא־נִבְקַ֖ע עָנָ֣ן תַּחְתָּֽם׃
He covers the face of his throne,[^9] spreading his cloud over it.
מְאַחֵ֥ז פְּנֵי־כִסֵּ֑ה פַּרְשֵׁ֖ז עָלָ֣יו עֲנָנֽוֹ׃
He has marked out a circle on the face of the waters,[^10] at the boundary between light and darkness.
חֹֽק־חָ֭ג עַל־פְּנֵי־מָ֑יִם עַד־תַּכְלִ֖ית א֣וֹר עִם־חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
The pillars of heaven tremble and are astounded at his rebuke.
עַמּוּדֵ֣י שָׁמַ֣יִם יְרוֹפָ֑פוּ וְ֝יִתְמְה֗וּ מִגַּעֲרָתֽוֹ׃
By his power he stilled[^11] the sea; by his understanding he shattered Rahab.[^12]
בְּ֭כֹחוֹ רָגַ֣ע הַיָּ֑ם *ובתובנתו **וּ֝בִתְבוּנָת֗וֹ מָ֣חַץ רָֽהַב׃
By his breath[^13] the heavens became clear; his hand pierced the fleeing serpent.[^14]
בְּ֭רוּחוֹ שָׁמַ֣יִם שִׁפְרָ֑ה חֹֽלֲלָ֥ה יָ֝ד֗וֹ נָחָ֥שׁ בָּרִֽיחַ׃
Look, these are only the edges of his ways;[^15] how faint is the whisper we hear of him![^16] But the thunder of his mighty deeds,[^17] who can understand?"
הֶן־אֵ֤לֶּה ׀ קְצ֬וֹת *דרכו **דְּרָכָ֗יו וּמַה־שֵּׁ֣מֶץ דָּ֭בָר נִשְׁמַע־בּ֑וֹ וְרַ֥עַם *גבורתו **גְּ֝בוּרוֹתָ֗יו מִ֣י יִתְבּוֹנָֽן׃ ס

n.1: Job is being sarcastic. In verses 2–4, *you* is singular: Job speaks to Bildad.
n.2: Hebrew *tushiyyah*, "sound wisdom", as in 5:12.
n.3: Literally "Whom have you told words?": either "To whom" or "With whose help".
n.4: Or "Whose spirit". Hebrew *neshamah*.
n.5: Hebrew *repha'im*, the dead in the world below (Psalm 88:11 (88:10 in most English Bibles); Isaiah 14:9). Some interpreters think verses 5–14 belong to Bildad's speech in chapter 25 (see the note at 25:1).
n.6: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.
n.7: Hebrew *Abaddon*, "Destruction", a name for the realm of the dead (28:22; 31:12; Proverbs 15:11).
n.8: Hebrew *tohu*, "emptiness, formlessness", the word in Genesis 1:2. *The north* (Hebrew *tsafon*) may be the northern sky, or the mountain of the gods in the far north (compare Isaiah 14:13).
n.9: Hebrew *kisseh*, a spelling of *kisse*, "throne". The same consonants can be read *keseh*, "full moon": "He covers the face of the full moon".
n.10: Literally "He has circled a limit on the face of the waters". The horizon is pictured as a circle drawn on the waters at the edge of the world (compare Proverbs 8:27).
n.11: Or "he stirred up". The Hebrew verb *raga* can mean either.
n.12: A sea monster, a figure of chaos (see 9:13).
n.13: Or "By his wind". Hebrew *ruach*.
n.14: Or "the gliding serpent". Isaiah 27:1 uses the same words of Leviathan.
n.15: The Hebrew text is written "his way" but read "his ways".
n.16: Literally "how small a whisper of a word is heard of him".
n.17: The Hebrew text is written "his might" but read "his mighty deeds".

v: Job took up his discourse again:[^1]
וַיֹּ֣סֶף אִ֭יּוֹב שְׂאֵ֥ת מְשָׁל֗וֹ וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"As surely as God lives, who has denied me justice,[^2] and the Almighty,[^3] who has made my soul bitter,
חַי אֵ֭ל הֵסִ֣יר מִשְׁפָּטִ֑י וְ֝שַׁדַּ֗י הֵמַ֥ר נַפְשִֽׁי׃
as long as my breath is in me, and the breath of God[^4] is in my nostrils,
כִּֽי־כָל־ע֣וֹד נִשְׁמָתִ֣י בִ֑י וְר֖וּחַ אֱל֣וֹהַּ בְּאַפִּֽי׃
my lips will not speak wickedness, and my tongue will not utter deceit.[^5]
אִם־תְּדַבֵּ֣רְנָה שְׂפָתַ֣י עַוְלָ֑ה וּ֝לְשׁוֹנִ֗י אִם־יֶהְגֶּ֥ה רְמִיָּֽה׃
Far be it from me to declare that you are right![^6] Until I breathe my last, I will not give up my integrity.
חָלִ֣ילָה לִּי֮ אִם־אַצְדִּ֢יק אֶ֫תְכֶ֥ם עַד־אֶגְוָ֑ע לֹא־אָסִ֖יר תֻּמָּתִ֣י מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
I hold fast to my righteousness and will not let it go; my heart does not reproach me for any of my days.
בְּצִדְקָתִ֣י הֶ֭חֱזַקְתִּי וְלֹ֣א אַרְפֶּ֑הָ לֹֽא־יֶחֱרַ֥ף לְ֝בָבִ֗י מִיָּמָֽי׃
May my enemy be like the wicked, and the one who rises against me like the unjust.
יְהִ֣י כְ֭רָשָׁע אֹ֣יְבִ֑י וּמִתְקוֹמְמִ֥י כְעַוָּֽל׃
For what hope does the godless have when he is cut off,[^7] when God takes away his life?[^8]
כִּ֤י מַה־תִּקְוַ֣ת חָ֭נֵף כִּ֣י יִבְצָ֑ע כִּ֤י יֵ֖שֶׁל אֱל֣וֹהַּ נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
Will God hear his cry when trouble comes upon him?
הַֽ֭צַעֲקָתוֹ יִשְׁמַ֥ע ׀ אֵ֑ל כִּֽי־תָב֖וֹא עָלָ֣יו צָרָֽה׃
Will he take delight in the Almighty? Will he call on God at all times?
אִם־עַל־שַׁדַּ֥י יִתְעַנָּ֑ג יִקְרָ֖א אֱל֣וֹהַּ בְּכָל־עֵֽת׃
I will teach you about the power[^9] of God; I will not hide what is with the Almighty.
אוֹרֶ֣ה אֶתְכֶ֣ם בְּיַד־אֵ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר עִם־שַׁ֝דַּ֗י לֹ֣א אֲכַחֵֽד׃
Look, all of you have seen it yourselves. Why then do you talk such empty nonsense?[^10]
הֵן־אַתֶּ֣ם כֻּלְּכֶ֣ם חֲזִיתֶ֑ם וְלָמָּה־זֶּ֝֗ה הֶ֣בֶל תֶּהְבָּֽלוּ׃
This is the portion of a wicked person from God, the inheritance that the ruthless receive from the Almighty:[^11]
זֶ֤ה ׀ חֵֽלֶק־אָדָ֖ם רָשָׁ֥ע ׀ עִם־אֵ֑ל וְֽנַחֲלַ֥ת עָ֝רִיצִ֗ים מִשַׁדַּ֥י יִקָּֽחוּ׃
If his children are many, it is for the sword, and his offspring will not have enough bread.
אִם־יִרְבּ֣וּ בָנָ֣יו לְמוֹ־חָ֑רֶב וְ֝צֶאֱצָאָ֗יו לֹ֣א יִשְׂבְּעוּ־לָֽחֶם׃
Those who survive him[^12] will be buried by the plague,[^13] and his widows will not weep.[^14]
*שרידו **שְׂ֭רִידָיו בַּמָּ֣וֶת יִקָּבֵ֑רוּ וְ֝אַלְמְנֹתָ֗יו לֹ֣א תִבְכֶּֽינָה׃
Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up clothing like clay,
אִם־יִצְבֹּ֣ר כֶּעָפָ֣ר כָּ֑סֶף וְ֝כַחֹ֗מֶר יָכִ֥ין מַלְבּֽוּשׁ׃
he may pile it up, but the righteous will wear it, and the innocent will divide the silver.
יָ֭כִין וְצַדִּ֣יק יִלְבָּ֑שׁ וְ֝כֶ֗סֶף נָקִ֥י יַחֲלֹֽק׃
He builds his house like a moth,[^15] like a hut that a watchman makes.
בָּנָ֣ה כָעָ֣שׁ בֵּית֑וֹ וּ֝כְסֻכָּ֗ה עָשָׂ֥ה נֹצֵֽר׃
He lies down rich, but will not do so again;[^16] he opens his eyes, and it is gone.[^17]
עָשִׁ֣יר יִ֭שְׁכַּב וְלֹ֣א יֵאָסֵ֑ף עֵינָ֖יו פָּקַ֣ח וְאֵינֶֽנּוּ׃
Terrors overtake him like a flood;[^18] in the night a storm wind carries him off.
תַּשִּׂיגֵ֣הוּ כַ֭מַּיִם בַּלָּה֑וֹת לַ֝֗יְלָה גְּנָבַ֥תּוּ סוּפָֽה׃
The east wind lifts him up, and he is gone; it sweeps him out of his place.
יִשָּׂאֵ֣הוּ קָדִ֣ים וְיֵלַ֑ךְ וִֽ֝ישָׂעֲרֵ֗הוּ מִמְּקֹמֽוֹ׃
It hurls itself at him without pity;[^19] he flees headlong from its power.
וְיַשְׁלֵ֣ךְ עָ֭לָיו וְלֹ֣א יַחְמֹ֑ל מִ֝יָּד֗וֹ בָּר֥וֹחַ יִבְרָֽח׃
It claps its hands at him and hisses at him from its place.[^20]
יִשְׂפֹּ֣ק עָלֵ֣ימוֹ כַפֵּ֑ימוֹ וְיִשְׁרֹ֥ק עָ֝לָ֗יו מִמְּקֹמֽוֹ׃

n.1: Literally "And Job again lifted up his *mashal* and said". Hebrew *mashal* usually means a proverb or a poem; here, a solemn speech. Also in 29:1. This new heading, at the point where Zophar would be expected to speak, is one reason some think the order of this third round of speeches has been disturbed (see the note at 25:1).
n.2: Literally "who has taken away my justice". Hebrew *mishpat*: justice, the right owed to me in my case. *As surely as God lives* is the form of an oath (literally "God lives").
n.3: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain. Also in verses 10, 11 and 13.
n.4: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job. Also in verses 8 and 10. *Breath* is Hebrew *ruach*, "breath, spirit".
n.5: Literally "if my lips speak wickedness, if my tongue utters deceit …", the form of a solemn oath: "may God punish me if I do".
n.6: Literally "to declare you righteous". Here *you* is plural: Job speaks to the three friends.
n.7: Hebrew *yivtsa*, "he cuts off" or "he makes gain". Or "however much he has gained".
n.8: Literally "when God draws out his soul". Hebrew *yeshel*, a rare verb, perhaps "draws out" or "takes away".
n.9: Literally "the hand".
n.10: Literally "Why then do you become empty with emptiness?" Hebrew *hevel*, "breath, vapor": what has no substance.
n.11: Compare Zophar's words in 20:29. Some interpreters think verses 13–23 are Zophar's third speech, which is otherwise missing (see the note at 25:1). Others take them as Job turning his friends' teaching back on them, or as Job's own view of what the wicked deserve. In the Hebrew text they stand within Job's speech.
n.12: The Hebrew text is written "his survivor" but read "his survivors".
n.13: Literally "will be buried in death". *Death* here probably means plague (compare Jeremiah 15:2).
n.14: Perhaps because no proper mourning rites can be held (compare Psalm 78:64).
n.15: Hebrew *ash*, "moth", perhaps meaning its cocoon.
n.16: Literally "he will not be gathered". The Greek Septuagint reads "he will not add (to it)", that is, he lies down rich for the last time.
n.17: Literally "and he is not": either his wealth is gone, or he himself.
n.18: Literally "like waters".
n.19: Or "He (God) hurls at him without pity". The subject is not stated.
n.20: Clapping the hands and hissing were gestures of scorn (Lamentations 2:15). The subject may be the wind, or people who see his fall: "People clap their hands at him and hiss at him from his place".

v: "Surely there is a mine for silver,[^1] and a place for the gold that people refine.
כִּ֤י יֵ֣שׁ לַכֶּ֣סֶף מוֹצָ֑א וּ֝מָק֗וֹם לַזָּהָ֥ב יָזֹֽקּוּ׃
Iron is taken from the dust, and copper[^2] is smelted from stone.
בַּ֭רְזֶל מֵעָפָ֣ר יֻקָּ֑ח וְ֝אֶ֗בֶן יָצ֥וּק נְחוּשָֽׁה׃
People put an end to darkness;[^3] they search out the farthest limits, for the stone that lies in gloom and deep darkness.[^4]
קֵ֤ץ ׀ שָׂ֤ם לַחֹ֗שֶׁךְ וּֽלְכָל־תַּ֭כְלִית ה֣וּא חוֹקֵ֑ר אֶ֖בֶן אֹ֣פֶל וְצַלְמָֽוֶת׃
They open a shaft far from where anyone lives, in places forgotten by any foot; far from other people they dangle and sway.[^5]
פָּ֤רַץ נַ֨חַל ׀ מֵֽעִם־גָּ֗ר הַֽנִּשְׁכָּחִ֥ים מִנִּי־רָ֑גֶל דַּ֖לּוּ מֵאֱנ֣וֹשׁ נָֽעוּ׃
The earth, from which bread comes, is turned upside down beneath, as if by fire.[^6]
אֶ֗רֶץ מִמֶּ֥נָּה יֵֽצֵא־לָ֑חֶם וְ֝תַחְתֶּ֗יהָ נֶהְפַּ֥ךְ כְּמוֹ־אֵֽשׁ׃
Its stones are the place of sapphires,[^7] and it holds dust of gold.[^8]
מְקוֹם־סַפִּ֥יר אֲבָנֶ֑יהָ וְעַפְרֹ֖ת זָהָ֣ב לֽוֹ׃
No bird of prey knows that path; the falcon's eye has not seen it.
נָ֭תִיב לֹֽא־יְדָ֣עוֹ עָ֑יִט וְלֹ֥א שְׁ֝זָפַ֗תּוּ עֵ֣ין אַיָּֽה׃
Proud beasts[^9] have not trodden it; no lion has passed over it.
לֹֽא־הִדְרִיכֻ֥הוּ בְנֵי־שָׁ֑חַץ לֹֽא־עָדָ֖ה עָלָ֣יו שָֽׁחַל׃
People put their hand to the flint and overturn mountains from their roots.
בַּֽ֭חַלָּמִישׁ שָׁלַ֣ח יָד֑וֹ הָפַ֖ךְ מִשֹּׁ֣רֶשׁ הָרִֽים׃
They cut channels[^10] through the rocks, and their eyes see every precious thing.
בַּ֭צּוּרוֹת יְאֹרִ֣ים בִּקֵּ֑עַ וְכָל־יְ֝קָ֗ר רָאֲתָ֥ה עֵינֽוֹ׃
They dam up the sources of the rivers[^11] and bring hidden things out into the light.
מִ֭בְּכִי נְהָר֣וֹת חִבֵּ֑שׁ וְ֝תַעֲלֻמָ֗הּ יֹ֣צִא אֽוֹר׃ פ
But wisdom, where can it be found? Where is the place of understanding?
וְֽ֭הַחָכְמָה מֵאַ֣יִן תִּמָּצֵ֑א וְאֵ֥י זֶ֝ה מְק֣וֹם בִּינָֽה׃
No mortal knows its worth;[^12] it is not found in the land of the living.
לֹא־יָדַ֣ע אֱנ֣וֹשׁ עֶרְכָּ֑הּ וְלֹ֥א תִ֝מָּצֵ֗א בְּאֶ֣רֶץ הֽ͏ַחַיִּֽים׃
The deep[^13] says, 'It is not in me,' and the sea says, 'It is not with me.'
תְּה֣וֹם אָ֭מַר לֹ֣א בִי־הִ֑יא וְיָ֥ם אָ֝מַ֗ר אֵ֣ין עִמָּדִֽי׃
It cannot be bought with solid gold,[^14] and its price cannot be weighed out in silver.
לֹא־יֻתַּ֣ן סְג֣וֹר תַּחְתֶּ֑יהָ וְלֹ֥א יִ֝שָּׁקֵ֗ל כֶּ֣סֶף מְחִירָֽהּ׃
It cannot be valued in the gold of Ophir,[^15] in precious onyx[^16] or sapphire.
לֹֽא־תְ֭סֻלֶּה בְּכֶ֣תֶם אוֹפִ֑יר בְּשֹׁ֖הַם יָקָ֣ר וְסַפִּֽיר׃
Gold and glass[^17] cannot compare with it, nor can it be exchanged for vessels of fine gold.
לֹא־יַעַרְכֶ֣נָּה זָ֭הָב וּזְכוֹכִ֑ית וּתְמ֖וּרָתָ֣הּ כְּלִי־פָֽז׃
Coral and crystal are not worth mentioning; the price of wisdom is above pearls.[^18]
רָאמ֣וֹת וְ֭גָבִישׁ לֹ֣א יִזָּכֵ֑ר וּמֶ֥שֶׁךְ חָ֝כְמָ֗ה מִפְּנִינִֽים׃
The topaz of Cush[^19] cannot compare with it; it cannot be valued in pure gold.
לֹֽא־יַ֭עַרְכֶנָּה פִּטְדַת־כּ֑וּשׁ בְּכֶ֥תֶם טָ֝ה֗וֹר לֹ֣א תְסֻלֶּֽה׃ פ
Where then does wisdom come from? Where is the place of understanding?
וְֽ֭הַחָכְמָה מֵאַ֣יִן תָּב֑וֹא וְאֵ֥י זֶ֝֗ה מְק֣וֹם בִּינָֽה׃
It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing, concealed even from the birds of the sky.
וְֽ֭נֶעֶלְמָה מֵעֵינֵ֣י כָל־חָ֑י וּמֵע֖וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם נִסְתָּֽרָה׃
Abaddon[^20] and Death say, 'With our ears we have heard a rumor of it.'
אֲבַדּ֣וֹן וָ֭מָוֶת אָ֣מְר֑וּ בְּ֝אָזְנֵ֗ינוּ שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ שִׁמְעָֽהּ׃
God understands the way to it; he knows its place.
אֱ֭לֹהִים הֵבִ֣ין דַּרְכָּ֑הּ וְ֝ה֗וּא יָדַ֥ע אֶת־מְקוֹמָֽהּ׃
For he looks to the ends of the earth; he sees everything under the heavens.
כִּי־ה֭וּא לִקְצוֹת־הָאָ֣רֶץ יַבִּ֑יט תַּ֖חַת כָּל־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם יִרְאֶֽה׃
When he gave the wind its weight and measured out the waters,
לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת לָר֣וּחַ מִשְׁקָ֑ל וּ֝מַ֗יִם תִּכֵּ֥ן בְּמִדָּֽה׃
when he made a decree for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt,[^21]
בַּעֲשֹׂת֣וֹ לַמָּטָ֣ר חֹ֑ק וְ֝דֶ֗רֶךְ לַחֲזִ֥יז קֹלֽוֹת׃
then he saw it and declared it;[^22] he established it and searched it out.
אָ֣ז רָ֭אָהּ וַֽיְסַפְּרָ֑הּ הֱ֝כִינָ֗הּ וְגַם־חֲקָרָֽהּ׃
And he said to humankind, 'Look, the fear of the Lord,[^23] that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding.'"[^24]
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר ׀ לָֽאָדָ֗ם הֵ֤ן יִרְאַ֣ת אֲ֭דֹנָי הִ֣יא חָכְמָ֑ה וְס֖וּר מֵרָ֣ע בִּינָֽה׃ ס

n.1: Chapter 28 is a poem on wisdom. It has no heading of its own, so in the text as it stands it continues Job's speech from chapter 27 (compare 29:1). Its calm, reflective tone has led many interpreters to think of it as an independent poem, perhaps spoken by the narrator. *Mine* is literally "a place where it comes out" (Hebrew *motsa*).
n.2: Or "bronze". Hebrew *nechushah*.
n.3: Literally "He sets an end to darkness": the miner, who brings light into the dark.
n.4: Hebrew *tsalmavet*, "deep darkness", traditionally read as "the shadow of death".
n.5: The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain. Literally "He breaks open a wadi away from the sojourner; the ones forgotten by the foot, they hang low; away from mortals they sway". It probably describes miners lowered on ropes into the shafts.
n.6: Perhaps the fire used to crack rock in mining.
n.7: Hebrew *sappir*, probably lapis lazuli, a deep blue stone flecked with gold. Also in verse 16.
n.8: Or "and it (the sapphire) has flecks of gold".
n.9: Literally "the sons of pride", probably the great wild animals (compare 41:26 (41:34 in most English Bibles)).
n.10: Hebrew *ye'orim*, a word used of the channels of the Nile; here tunnels or water channels in a mine.
n.11: The Hebrew vowel points read "From the weeping of the rivers he binds", that is, he stops the water from seeping into the mine. The same consonants can be read "the sources of the rivers" (compare "the springs of the sea", 38:16).
n.12: Or "its place in order". The Greek Septuagint reads "its way".
n.13: Hebrew *tehom*, the deep waters under the earth (Genesis 1:2).
n.14: Hebrew *segor*, a rare word for gold, probably "pure" or "solid" gold. Verses 15–19 use several words for gold and precious stones, some of which cannot be identified with certainty.
n.15: A region famous for its fine gold, perhaps in southern Arabia or East Africa (1 Kings 9:28).
n.16: Hebrew *shoham*, a precious stone that cannot be identified with certainty.
n.17: Hebrew *zekhukhit*, a word found only here. Glass was costly in the ancient world.
n.18: Hebrew *ramot*, *gavish* and *peninim*, precious things that cannot be identified with certainty. *Peninim* may be red coral (Lamentations 4:7) or pearls. *Price* is literally "drawing out", perhaps the acquiring of it.
n.19: Hebrew *pitdah*, a precious stone, perhaps topaz or chrysolite. *Cush* is usually the region south of Egypt (ancient Nubia).
n.20: Hebrew *Abaddon*, "Destruction", a name for the realm of the dead (see 26:6).
n.21: Literally "for the flash of the thunders".
n.23: Hebrew *Adonai*, "Lord", used of God only here in Job.
n.24: The words echo the description of Job in 1:1: he "feared God and turned away from evil". Compare Proverbs 1:7; 9:10.

v: Job took up his discourse again:[^1]
וַיֹּ֣סֶף אִ֭יּוֹב שְׂאֵ֥ת מְשָׁל֗וֹ וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"If only I were as in the months gone by, as in the days when God[^2] watched over me,
מִֽי־יִתְּנֵ֥נִי כְיַרְחֵי־קֶ֑דֶם כִּ֝ימֵ֗י אֱל֣וֹהַּ יִשְׁמְרֵֽנִי׃
when his lamp shone above my head, and by his light I walked through darkness;
בְּהִלּ֣וֹ נֵ֭רוֹ עֲלֵ֣י רֹאשִׁ֑י לְ֝אוֹרוֹ אֵ֣לֶךְ חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
as I was in the days of my prime,[^3] when the friendship[^4] of God was over my tent;
כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר הָ֭יִיתִי בִּימֵ֣י חָרְפִּ֑י בְּס֥וֹד אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַּ עֲלֵ֣י אָהֳלִֽי׃
when the Almighty[^5] was still with me, and my children[^6] were all around me;
בְּע֣וֹד שַׁ֭דַּי עִמָּדִ֑י סְבִ֖יבוֹתַ֣י נְעָרָֽי׃
when my steps were bathed in cream,[^7] and the rock poured out streams of oil for me!
בִּרְחֹ֣ץ הֲלִיכַ֣י בְּחֵמָ֑ה וְצ֥וּר יָצ֥וּק עִ֝מָּדִ֗י פַּלְגֵי־שָֽׁמֶן׃
When I went out to the gate of the city[^8] and set up my seat in the square,
בְּצֵ֣אתִי שַׁ֣עַר עֲלֵי־קָ֑רֶת בָּ֝רְח֗וֹב אָכִ֥ין מוֹשָׁבִֽי׃
the young men saw me and drew back,[^9] and the old men rose and stood;
רָא֣וּנִי נְעָרִ֣ים וְנֶחְבָּ֑אוּ וִֽ֝ישִׁישִׁים קָ֣מוּ עָמָֽדוּ׃
officials stopped talking[^10] and put their hands over their mouths;
שָׂ֭רִים עָצְר֣וּ בְמִלִּ֑ים וְ֝כַ֗ף יָשִׂ֥ימוּ לְפִיהֶֽם׃
the voices of the nobles were hushed, and their tongues stuck to the roof of their mouths.
קוֹל־נְגִידִ֥ים נֶחְבָּ֑אוּ וּ֝לְשׁוֹנָ֗ם לְחִכָּ֥ם דָּבֵֽקָה׃
For any ear that heard me called me blessed, and any eye that saw me spoke well of me,[^11]
כִּ֤י אֹ֣זֶן שָׁ֭מְעָה וַֽתְּאַשְּׁרֵ֑נִי וְעַ֥ין רָ֝אֲתָ֗ה וַתְּעִידֵֽנִי׃
because I rescued the poor who cried for help, and the orphan who had no one to help him.
כִּֽי־אֲ֭מַלֵּט עָנִ֣י מְשַׁוֵּ֑עַ וְ֝יָת֗וֹם וְֽלֹא־עֹזֵ֥ר לֽוֹ׃
The blessing of the one who was perishing came upon me, and I made the widow's heart sing for joy.
בִּרְכַּ֣ת אֹ֭בֵד עָלַ֣י תָּבֹ֑א וְלֵ֖ב אַלְמָנָ֣ה אַרְנִֽן׃
I put on righteousness, and it clothed me;[^12] my justice was like a robe and a turban.
צֶ֣דֶק לָ֭בַשְׁתִּי וַיִּלְבָּשֵׁ֑נִי כִּֽמְעִ֥יל וְ֝צָנִ֗יף מִשְׁפָּטִֽי׃
I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.
עֵינַ֣יִם הָ֭יִיתִי לַֽעִוֵּ֑ר וְרַגְלַ֖יִם לַפִּסֵּ֣חַ אָֽנִי׃
I was a father to the needy, and I looked into the case of the stranger.[^13]
אָ֣ב אָ֭נֹכִֽי לָֽאֶבְיוֹנִ֑ים וְרִ֖ב לֹא־יָדַ֣עְתִּי אֶחְקְרֵֽהוּ׃
I broke the jaws of the unjust and made them drop their prey from their teeth.
וָֽ֭אֲשַׁבְּרָה מְתַלְּע֣וֹת עַוָּ֑ל וּ֝מִשִּׁנָּ֗יו אַשְׁלִ֥יךְ טָֽרֶף׃
Then I thought, 'I will die in my nest,[^14] and I will multiply my days like the sand.[^15]
וָ֭אֹמַר עִם־קִנִּ֣י אֶגְוָ֑ע וְ֝כַח֗וֹל אַרְבֶּ֥ה יָמִֽים׃
My roots will be open to the water, and the dew will lie all night on my branches.
שָׁרְשִׁ֣י פָת֣וּחַ אֱלֵי־מָ֑יִם וְ֝טַ֗ל יָלִ֥ין בִּקְצִירֽ͏ִי׃
My glory will stay fresh with me,[^16] and my bow will be renewed in my hand.'
כְּ֭בוֹדִי חָדָ֣שׁ עִמָּדִ֑י וְ֝קַשְׁתִּ֗י בְּיָדִ֥י תַחֲלִֽיף׃
People listened to me and waited; they kept silent for my counsel.
לִֽי־שָׁמְע֥וּ וְיִחֵ֑לּוּ וְ֝יִדְּמ֗וּ לְמ֣וֹ עֲצָתִֽי׃
After I had spoken, they did not speak again; my words fell on them drop by drop.[^17]
אַחֲרֵ֣י דְ֭בָרִי לֹ֣א יִשְׁנ֑וּ וְ֝עָלֵ֗ימוֹ תִּטֹּ֥ף מִלָּתִֽי׃
They waited for me as for the rain; they opened their mouths as for the spring rain.[^18]
וְיִֽחֲל֣וּ כַמָּטָ֣ר לִ֑י וּ֝פִיהֶ֗ם פָּעֲר֥וּ לְמַלְקֽוֹשׁ׃
When I smiled at them, they could hardly believe it;[^19] they did not let the light of my face fall.[^20]
אֶשְׂחַ֣ק אֲ֭לֵהֶם לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֑ינוּ וְא֥וֹר פָּ֝נַ֗י לֹ֣א יַפִּילֽוּן׃
I chose the way for them and sat as their chief; I lived like a king among his troops, like one who comforts mourners.
אֶֽבֲחַ֣ר דַּרְכָּם֮ וְאֵשֵׁ֢ב רֹ֥אשׁ וְ֭אֶשְׁכּוֹן כְּמֶ֣לֶךְ בַּגְּד֑וּד כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר אֲבֵלִ֣ים יְנַחֵֽם׃

n.1: Literally "And Job again lifted up his *mashal* and said" (see 27:1).
n.2: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job. Also in verse 4.
n.3: Literally "the days of my autumn", the season of harvest and fullness.
n.4: Hebrew *sod*, "intimate counsel, close friendship".
n.5: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain.
n.6: Or "my young men", "my servants". Hebrew *ne'arim*, as in 1:19.
n.7: Hebrew *chemah*, "curds, butter": a picture of great abundance.
n.8: Literally "to the gate, up to the city". Elders sat at the city gate to hear cases and give judgment.
n.9: Literally "hid themselves".
n.10: Literally "held back words".
n.11: Literally "testified for me".
n.12: Literally "and it clothed itself with me".
n.13: Literally "and the case I did not know I searched out": either the case of someone I did not know, or a case I did not yet understand.
n.14: That is, at home among my family.
n.15: Or "like the phoenix". Hebrew *chol* usually means "sand", but an ancient Jewish tradition takes it here as the name of a long-lived bird, the phoenix.
n.16: Literally "My glory is new with me". Hebrew *kavod*: honor, dignity, vigor.
n.17: Literally "and my word dripped on them", like rain.
n.18: The late rain of spring, which ripened the crops before harvest.
n.19: Literally "I laughed toward them; they did not believe". Or "I smiled at them when they had lost confidence".
n.20: The meaning of this line is uncertain. Perhaps "they did not cast down the light of my face", that is, they did nothing to lose my favor.

v: "But now they laugh at me, those younger than I, whose fathers I would have refused to put with the dogs of my flock.
וְעַתָּ֤ה ׀ שָֽׂחֲק֣וּ עָלַי֮ צְעִירִ֥ים מִמֶּ֗נִּי לְיָ֫מִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־מָאַ֥סְתִּי אֲבוֹתָ֑ם לָ֝שִׁ֗ית עִם־כַּלְבֵ֥י צֹאנִֽי׃
What use to me was the strength of their hands? Their vigor[^1] had perished.
גַּם־כֹּ֣חַ יְ֭דֵיהֶם לָ֣מָּה לִּ֑י עָ֝לֵ֗ימוֹ אָ֣בַד כָּֽלַח׃
Gaunt from want and hunger, they gnaw the dry ground,[^2] in the gloom of desolation and waste.[^3]
בְּחֶ֥סֶר וּבְכָפָ֗ן גַּ֫לְמ֥וּד הַֽעֹרְקִ֥ים צִיָּ֑ה אֶ֝֗מֶשׁ שׁוֹאָ֥ה וּמְשֹׁאָֽה׃
They pluck saltwort[^4] among the bushes, and the root of the broom bush is their food.[^5]
הַקֹּטְפִ֣ים מַלּ֣וּחַ עֲלֵי־שִׂ֑יחַ וְשֹׁ֖רֶשׁ רְתָמִ֣ים לַחְמָֽם׃
They are driven out from the community;[^6] people shout after them as after a thief.
מִן־גֵּ֥ו יְגֹרָ֑שׁוּ יָרִ֥יעוּ עָ֝לֵ֗ימוֹ כַּגַּנָּֽב׃
They have to live in the gullies of the wadis, in holes in the ground and among the rocks.
בַּעֲר֣וּץ נְחָלִ֣ים לִשְׁכֹּ֑ן חֹרֵ֖י עָפָ֣ר וְכֵפִֽים׃
Among the bushes they bray;[^7] under the nettles they huddle together.
בֵּין־שִׂיחִ֥ים יִנְהָ֑קוּ תַּ֖חַת חָר֣וּל יְסֻפָּֽחוּ׃
A senseless brood, a nameless brood,[^8] they were whipped out of the land.
בְּֽנֵי־נָ֭בָל גַּם־בְּנֵ֣י בְלִי־שֵׁ֑ם נִ֝כְּא֗וּ מִן־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
And now I have become their song;[^9] I have become a byword to them.
וְ֭עַתָּה נְגִינָתָ֣ם הָיִ֑יתִי וָאֱהִ֖י לָהֶ֣ם לְמִלָּֽה׃
They detest me; they keep their distance from me; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.
תִּֽ֭עֲבוּנִי רָ֣חֲקוּ מֶ֑נִּי וּ֝מִפָּנַ֗י לֹא־חָ֥שְׂכוּ רֹֽק׃
Because he has loosened my cord[^10] and humbled me, they have thrown off all restraint before me.[^11]
כִּֽי־*יתרו **יִתְרִ֣י פִ֭תַּח וַיְעַנֵּ֑נִי וְ֝רֶ֗סֶן מִפָּנַ֥י שִׁלֵּֽחוּ׃
On my right the rabble[^12] rise up; they push my feet away[^13] and build their roads of ruin against me.[^14]
עַל־יָמִין֮ פִּרְחַ֢ח יָ֫ק֥וּמוּ רַגְלַ֥י שִׁלֵּ֑חוּ וַיָּסֹ֥לּוּ עָ֝לַ֗י אָרְח֥וֹת אֵידָֽם׃
They tear up my path; they profit from my disaster;[^15] no one holds them back.[^16]
נָתְס֗וּ נְֽתִיבָ֫תִ֥י לְהַוָּתִ֥י יֹעִ֑ילוּ לֹ֖א עֹזֵ֣ר לָֽמוֹ׃
As through a wide breach they come; amid the crash[^17] they roll in.
כְּפֶ֣רֶץ רָחָ֣ב יֶאֱתָ֑יוּ תַּ֥חַת שֹׁ֝אָ֗ה הִתְגַּלְגָּֽלוּ׃
Terrors are turned against me; they chase away my dignity[^18] like the wind, and my safety has passed away like a cloud.
הָהְפַּ֥ךְ עָלַ֗י בַּלָּ֫ה֥וֹת תִּרְדֹּ֣ף כָּ֭רוּחַ נְדִבָתִ֑י וּ֝כְעָ֗ב עָבְרָ֥ה יְשֻׁעָתִֽי׃
And now my life is poured out within me;[^19] days of affliction have taken hold of me.
וְעַתָּ֗ה עָ֭לַי תִּשְׁתַּפֵּ֣ךְ נַפְשִׁ֑י יֹ֭אחֲז֣וּנִי יְמֵי־עֹֽנִי׃
At night my bones are pierced within me,[^20] and the pains that gnaw me take no rest.
לַ֗יְלָה עֲ֭צָמַי נִקַּ֣ר מֵעָלָ֑י וְ֝עֹרְקַ֗י לֹ֣א יִשְׁכָּבֽוּן׃
With great force my garment is disfigured; it binds me like the collar of my tunic.[^21]
בְּרָב־כֹּ֭חַ יִתְחַפֵּ֣שׂ לְבוּשִׁ֑י כְּפִ֖י כֻתָּנְתִּ֣י יַֽאַזְרֵֽנִי׃
He has thrown me into the mud,[^22] and I have become like dust and ashes.[^23]
הֹרָ֥נִי לַחֹ֑מֶר וָ֝אֶתְמַשֵּׁ֗ל כֶּעָפָ֥ר וָאֵֽפֶר׃
I cry to you for help, but you do not answer me; I stand up, and you just look at me.[^24]
אֲשַׁוַּ֣ע אֵ֭לֶיךָ וְלֹ֣א תַעֲנֵ֑נִי עָ֝מַ֗דְתִּי וַתִּתְבֹּ֥נֶן בִּֽי׃
You have turned cruel to me; with the might of your hand you attack me.[^25]
תֵּהָפֵ֣ךְ לְאַכְזָ֣ר לִ֑י בְּעֹ֖צֶם יָדְךָ֣ תִשְׂטְמֵֽנִי׃
You lift me up on the wind and make me ride it; you melt me away, and all my success.[^26]
תִּשָּׂאֵ֣נִי אֶל־ר֖[d]וּחַ תַּרְכִּיבֵ֑נִי וּ֝תְמֹגְגֵ֗נִי *תשוה **תּוּשִׁיָּֽה׃
For I know you will bring me back to death,[^27] to the house appointed for all the living.
כִּֽי־יָ֭דַעְתִּי מָ֣וֶת תְּשִׁיבֵ֑נִי וּבֵ֖ית מוֹעֵ֣ד לְכָל־חָֽי׃
Yet does not one in ruins stretch out a hand, and in his disaster cry for help?[^28]
אַ֣ךְ לֹא־בְ֭עִי יִשְׁלַח־יָ֑ד אִם־בְּ֝פִיד֗וֹ לָהֶ֥ן שֽׁוּעַ׃
Did I not weep for the one whose life was hard?[^29] Was my soul not grieved for the needy?
אִם־לֹ֣א בָ֭כִיתִי לִקְשֵׁה־י֑וֹם עָֽגְמָ֥ה נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י לָאֶבְיֽוֹן׃
Yet when I hoped for good, evil came; when I waited for light, darkness came.
כִּ֤י ט֣וֹב קִ֭וִּיתִי וַיָּ֣בֹא רָ֑ע וַֽאֲיַחֲלָ֥ה לְ֝א֗וֹר וַיָּ֥בֹא אֹֽפֶל׃
My insides are in turmoil and never still;[^30] days of affliction confront me.
מֵעַ֖י רֻתְּח֥וּ וְלֹא־דָ֗מּוּ קִדְּמֻ֥נִי יְמֵי־עֹֽנִי׃
I go about darkened, but not by the sun;[^31] I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.
קֹדֵ֣ר הִ֭לַּכְתִּי בְּלֹ֣א חַמָּ֑ה קַ֖מְתִּי בַקָּהָ֣ל אֲשַׁוֵּֽעַ׃
I have become a brother to jackals and a companion to ostriches.[^32]
אָ֭ח הָיִ֣יתִי לְתַנִּ֑ים וְ֝רֵ֗עַ לִבְנ֥וֹת יַעֲנָֽה׃
My skin has turned black and peels from me;[^33] my bones burn with fever.[^34]
ע֭וֹרִי שָׁחַ֣ר מֵעָלָ֑י וְעַצְמִי־חָ֝֗רָה מִנִּי־חֹֽרֶב׃
My lyre is turned to mourning, and my pipe to the sound of weeping.
וַיְהִ֣י לְ֭אֵבֶל כִּנֹּרִ֑י וְ֝עֻגָבִ֗י לְק֣וֹל בֹּכִֽים׃

n.1: Hebrew *kelach*, a rare word, perhaps "full vigor" or "ripe old age", as in 5:26.
n.2: Or "they flee to the dry ground". Hebrew *orqim*, a rare word.
n.3: Literally "the yesterday (or "night") of ruin and devastation". The meaning of this line is uncertain.
n.4: Hebrew *malluach*, a salty plant that grows in the desert.
n.5: Literally "their bread". Broom roots are bitter and were mostly used as fuel (Psalm 120:4). The same consonants can be read "to warm themselves".
n.6: Literally "from the midst". Hebrew *gev*, a rare word.
n.7: Like hungry wild donkeys (compare 6:5).
n.8: Literally "sons of a fool, also sons of no name".
n.9: That is, a mocking song.
n.10: *He* is God, though the Hebrew does not name him. *My cord* is perhaps my bowstring (compare 29:20) or my tent cord (compare 4:21). The Hebrew text is written "his cord" but read "my cord". With "his cord", the line may mean "each of them has loosened his cord (his restraint) and humbled me".
n.11: Literally "they have let loose the bridle before me".
n.12: Hebrew *pirchach*, a word found only here, perhaps "brood" or "rabble".
n.13: Literally "they send away my feet". The meaning is uncertain.
n.14: Like an army building siege ramps against a city (19:12).
n.15: Literally "they help toward my disaster".
n.16: Literally "there is no helper for them": perhaps "they need no one's help". The meaning is uncertain.
n.17: Hebrew *sho'ah*, "ruin, storm", the word translated "desolation" in verse 3.
n.18: Hebrew *nedivah*, "nobility, honor".
n.19: Literally "my soul pours itself out upon me".
n.20: Literally "The night pierces my bones from upon me".
n.21: The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain. *Is disfigured* is literally "disguises itself". Some scholars read "seizes my garment", with a small change to the Hebrew, with God as the subject: "With great force he seizes my garment; he grips me by the collar of my tunic".
n.23: The same pair of words, "dust and ashes", is used in 42:6 (compare Genesis 18:27).
n.25: Hebrew *satam*, "bear a grudge against, persecute", a verb close to *satan*, "accuser".
n.26: The Hebrew text is written *teshuwwah*, "(in) the roar of the storm", but read *tushiyyah*, "success" or "sound wisdom", as in 5:12. With the written form: "you toss me about in the roar of the storm".
n.27: Literally "you will return me to death".
n.28: The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain. Literally "Surely not into a heap of ruins does he stretch out a hand; if in his disaster, to them a cry for help". Or "Surely no one strikes a ruined man when he cries for help in his disaster".
n.30: Literally "My bowels boil and are not silent".
n.31: Literally "I go about dark, without the sun" (Hebrew *chammah*, "heat, sun"): darkened, perhaps in mourning, but not by the sun. Some scholars read *nechamah*, "comfort", for *chammah*, with a small change to the Hebrew: "I go about mourning, without comfort".
n.32: Hebrew *benot ya'anah*, perhaps "ostriches" or "eagle owls". Both jackals and these birds make mournful cries in desolate places (Micah 1:8).
n.33: Literally "My skin is black from upon me".

v: "I made a covenant with my eyes; how then could I gaze at a young woman?[^1]
בְּ֭רִית כָּרַ֣תִּי לְעֵינָ֑י וּמָ֥ה אֶ֝תְבּוֹנֵ֗ן עַל־בְּתוּלָֽה׃
What portion would I have from God[^2] above, what inheritance from the Almighty[^3] on high?
וּמֶ֤ה ׀ חֵ֣לֶק אֱל֣וֹהַּ מִמָּ֑עַל וְֽנַחֲלַ֥ת שַׁ֝דַּ֗י מִמְּרֹמִֽים׃
Is there not disaster for the unjust, and calamity for those who do wrong?
הֲלֹא־אֵ֥יד לְעַוָּ֑ל וְ֝נֵ֗כֶר לְפֹ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃
Does he not see my ways and count all my steps?
הֲלֹא־ה֭וּא יִרְאֶ֣ה דְרָכָ֑י וְֽכָל־צְעָדַ֥י יִסְפּֽוֹר׃
If I have walked with falsehood, or my foot has hurried after deceit,
אִם־הָלַ֥כְתִּי עִם־שָׁ֑וְא וַתַּ֖חַשׁ עַל־מִרְמָ֣ה רַגְלֽ͏ִי׃
let him weigh me on honest scales,[^4] and let God know my integrity.
יִשְׁקְלֵ֥נִי בְמֹאזְנֵי־צֶ֑דֶק וְיֵדַ֥ע אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַּ תֻּמָּתִֽי׃
If my steps have turned aside from the way, if my heart has followed my eyes, or if any stain has stuck to my hands,
אִ֥ם תִּטֶּ֣ה אַשֻּׁרִי֮ מִנִּ֢י הַ֫דָּ֥רֶךְ וְאַחַ֣ר עֵ֭ינַי הָלַ֣ךְ לִבִּ֑י וּ֝בְכַפַּ֗י דָּ֣בַק מֻאוּֽם׃ פ
then let me sow and another eat, and let my crops[^5] be uprooted.
אֶ֭זְרְעָה וְאַחֵ֣ר יֹאכֵ֑ל וְֽצֶאֱצָאַ֥י יְשֹׁרָֽשׁוּ׃
If my heart has been enticed by a woman, or I have lain in wait at my neighbor's door,
אִם־נִפְתָּ֣ה לִ֭בִּי עַל־אִשָּׁ֑ה וְעַל־פֶּ֖תַח רֵעִ֣י אָרָֽבְתִּי׃
then let my wife grind grain for another, and let other men kneel over her.[^6]
תִּטְחַ֣ן לְאַחֵ֣ר אִשְׁתִּ֑י וְ֝עָלֶ֗יהָ יִכְרְע֥וּן אֲחֵרִֽין׃
For that would be a shameful crime; it would be an offense for the judges to punish.[^7]
כִּי־*הוא **הִ֥יא זִמָּ֑ה *והיא **וְ֝ה֗וּא עָוֺ֥ן פְּלִילִֽים׃
For it is a fire that consumes all the way to Abaddon,[^8] and it would uproot all my harvest.
כִּ֤י אֵ֣שׁ הִ֭יא עַד־אֲבַדּ֣וֹן תֹּאכֵ֑ל וּֽבְכָל־תְּב֖וּאָתִ֣י תְשָׁרֵֽשׁ׃
If I have denied justice[^9] to my male or female servant[^10] when they brought a complaint against me,
אִם־אֶמְאַ֗ס מִשְׁפַּ֣ט עַ֭בְדִּי וַאֲמָתִ֑י בְּ֝רִבָ֗ם עִמָּדִֽי׃
what then could I do when God rises up? When he calls me to account, what could I answer him?
וּמָ֣ה אֶֽ֭עֱשֶׂה כִּֽי־יָק֣וּם אֵ֑ל וְכִֽי־יִ֝פְקֹ֗ד מָ֣ה אֲשִׁיבֶֽנּוּ׃
Did not the one who made me in the womb make them? Did not the same one form us in the womb?
הֲ‍ֽ֝ל[t]ֹא־בַ֭בֶּטֶן עֹשֵׂ֣נִי עָשָׂ֑הוּ וַ֝יְכֻנֶ֗נּוּ בָּרֶ֥חֶם אֶחָֽד׃
If I have withheld from the poor what they wanted, or let the widow's eyes grow dim with longing,[^11]
אִם־אֶ֭מְנַע מֵחֵ֣פֶץ דַּלִּ֑ים וְעֵינֵ֖י אַלְמָנָ֣ה אֲכַלֶּֽה׃
or eaten my bit of bread by myself, and the orphan has not eaten any of it,
וְאֹכַ֣ל פִּתִּ֣י לְבַדִּ֑י וְלֹא־אָכַ֖ל יָת֣וֹם מִמֶּֽנָּה׃
for from my youth the orphan grew up with me as with a father,[^12] and from my mother's womb I guided the widow,[^13]
כִּ֣י מִ֭נְּעוּרַי גְּדֵלַ֣נִי כְאָ֑ב וּמִבֶּ֖טֶן אִמִּ֣י אַנְחֶֽנָּה׃
if I have seen anyone perishing for lack of clothing, or the needy without covering,
אִם־אֶרְאֶ֣ה א֖וֹבֵד מִבְּלִ֣י לְב֑וּשׁ וְאֵ֥ין כְּ֝ס֗וּת לָאֶבְיֽוֹן׃
if his body[^14] has not blessed me, as he was warmed by the fleece of my sheep,
אִם־לֹ֣א בֵרֲכ֣וּנִי *חלצו **חֲלָצָ֑יו וּמִגֵּ֥ז כְּ֝בָשַׂי יִתְחַמָּֽם׃
if I have raised my hand against the orphan, because I saw I had support[^15] in the gate,
אִם־הֲנִיפ֣וֹתִי עַל־יָת֣וֹם יָדִ֑י כִּֽי־אֶרְאֶ֥ה בַ֝שַּׁ֗עַר עֶזְרָתִֽי׃
then let my shoulder fall from its socket,[^16] and let my arm be broken off at the elbow.[^17]
כְּ֭תֵפִי מִשִּׁכְמָ֣ה תִפּ֑וֹל וְ֝אֶזְרֹעִ֗י מִקָּנָ֥ה תִשָּׁבֵֽר׃
For disaster from God was a terror to me, and because of his majesty I could not do such things.[^18]
כִּ֤י פַ֣חַד אֵ֭לַי אֵ֣יד אֵ֑ל וּ֝מִשְּׂאֵת֗וֹ לֹ֣א אוּכָֽל׃
If I have made gold my confidence, or called fine gold my security,
אִם־שַׂ֣מְתִּי זָהָ֣ב כִּסְלִ֑י וְ֝לַכֶּ֗תֶם אָמַ֥רְתִּי מִבְטַחִֽי׃
if I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, or because my hand had gained so much,
אִם־אֶ֭שְׂמַח כִּי־רַ֣ב חֵילִ֑י וְכִֽי־כַ֝בִּ֗יר מָצְאָ֥ה יָדִֽי׃
if I have looked at the sun[^19] when it shone, or the moon moving in splendor,
אִם־אֶרְאֶ֣ה א֖וֹר כִּ֣י יָהֵ֑ל וְ֝יָרֵ֗חַ יָקָ֥ר הֹלֵֽךְ׃
and my heart has been secretly enticed, and my hand has thrown them a kiss,[^20]
וַיִּ֣פְתְּ בַּסֵּ֣תֶר לִבִּ֑י וַתִּשַּׁ֖ק יָדִ֣י לְפִֽי׃
this too would be an offense for the judges to punish, for I would have denied God above.
גַּם־ה֖[d]וּא עָוֺ֣ן פְּלִילִ֑י כִּֽי־כִחַ֖שְׁתִּי לָאֵ֣ל מִמָּֽעַל׃
If I have rejoiced at the ruin of one who hated me, or gloated when evil found him,
אִם־אֶ֭שְׂמַח בְּפִ֣יד מְשַׂנְאִ֑י וְ֝הִתְעֹרַ֗רְתִּי כִּֽי־מְצָ֥אוֹ רָֽע׃
I have not let my mouth[^21] sin by asking for his life with a curse.
וְלֹא־נָתַ֣תִּי לַחֲטֹ֣א חִכִּ֑י לִשְׁאֹ֖ל בְּאָלָ֣ה נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
If the men of my tent have not said, 'Who is there who has not had his fill of his meat?'[^22]
אִם־לֹ֣א אָ֭מְרוּ מְתֵ֣י אָהֳלִ֑י מִֽי־יִתֵּ֥ן מִ֝בְּשָׂר֗וֹ לֹ֣א נִשְׂבָּֽע׃
No stranger had to spend the night in the street; I opened my doors to the traveler.[^23]
בַּ֭חוּץ לֹא־יָלִ֣ין גֵּ֑ר דְּ֝לָתַ֗י לָאֹ֥רַח אֶפְתָּֽח׃
If I have covered my transgressions as others do,[^24] hiding my guilt in my bosom,
אִם־כִּסִּ֣יתִי כְאָדָ֣ם פְּשָׁעָ֑י לִטְמ֖וֹן בְּחֻבִּ֣י עֲוֺֽנִי׃
because I feared the great crowd, and the contempt of the clans terrified me, so that I kept silent and did not go out of my door—
כִּ֤י אֶֽעֱר֨וֹץ ׀ הָ֘מ֤וֹן רַבָּ֗ה וּבוּז־מִשְׁפָּח֥וֹת יְחִתֵּ֑נִי וָ֝אֶדֹּ֗ם לֹא־אֵ֥צֵא פָֽתַח׃
Oh, that I had someone to hear me! Here is my signature;[^25] let the Almighty answer me! Let my opponent write out his charge against me![^26]
מִ֤י יִתֶּן־לִ֨י ׀ שֹׁ֘מֵ֤עַֽ לִ֗י הֶן־תָּ֭וִי שַׁדַּ֣י יַעֲנֵ֑נִי וְסֵ֥פֶר כָּ֝תַ֗ב אִ֣ישׁ רִיבִֽי׃
Surely I would carry it on my shoulder; I would bind it on like a crown.[^27]
אִם־לֹ֣א עַל־שִׁ֭כְמִי אֶשָּׂאֶ֑נּוּ אֶֽעֶנְדֶ֖נּוּ עֲטָר֣וֹת לִֽי׃
I would give him an account of all my steps; like a prince I would approach him.
מִסְפַּ֣ר צְ֭עָדַי אַגִּידֶ֑נּוּ כְּמוֹ־נָ֝גִ֗יד אֲקָרֲבֶֽנּוּ׃
If my land has cried out against me, and its furrows have wept together,
אִם־עָ֭לַי אַדְמָתִ֣י תִזְעָ֑ק וְ֝יַ֗חַד תְּלָמֶ֥יהָ יִבְכָּיֽוּן׃
if I have eaten its produce[^28] without paying, or made its owners breathe their last,
אִם־כֹּ֭חָהּ אָכַ֣לְתִּי בְלִי־כָ֑סֶף וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ בְּעָלֶ֣יהָ הִפָּֽחְתִּי׃
then let thorns grow instead of wheat, and stinking weeds[^29] instead of barley." The words of Job are ended.[^30]
תַּ֤חַת חִטָּ֨ה ׀ יֵ֥צֵא ח֗וֹחַ וְתַֽחַת־שְׂעֹרָ֥ה בָאְשָׁ֑ה תַּ֝֗מּוּ דִּבְרֵ֥י אִיּֽוֹב׃ פ

n.1: Hebrew *betulah*, "a young woman, a virgin".
n.2: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job. Also in verse 6.
n.3: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain. Also in verse 35.
n.4: Literally "scales of righteousness".
n.5: Or "my descendants". Hebrew *tse'etsa'im*, "what comes out": produce, or offspring.
n.6: Grinding grain was the work of a slave woman. *Kneel over her* refers to sexual relations, and the first line may also be meant that way.
n.7: Literally "an iniquity of judges": a crime that the courts punish. Also in verse 28.
n.8: Hebrew *Abaddon*, "Destruction", a name for the realm of the dead (see 26:6).
n.9: Hebrew *mishpat*: justice, right, a legal case.
n.10: Or "slave".
n.11: Literally "made the eyes of the widow fail".
n.12: Literally "he grew me up as a father", a difficult phrase. Perhaps "he (the orphan) grew up with me as with a father", or "he (God) raised me like a father".
n.13: Literally "I guided her", the widow of verse 16: a way of saying that Job cared for widows all his life.
n.14: Literally "his loins".
n.15: Literally "my help": those who would take my side in court at the city gate.
n.16: Literally "from the shoulder blade".
n.17: Literally "from the reed", perhaps the upper arm bone.
n.18: Literally "and from his majesty I was not able".
n.19: Literally "the light".
n.20: Literally "and my hand has kissed my mouth", a gesture of worship to the sun and moon.
n.22: Literally "Who will give one who is not satisfied from his flesh?" Job's household could say that everyone had eaten their fill at his table.
n.23: The Hebrew vowel points read "to the road". The same consonants can be read "to the traveler".
n.24: Or "as Adam did" (compare Genesis 3:8–10). Hebrew *ke-adam*, "like a human being" or "like Adam".
n.25: Literally "Here is my *tav*". *Tav* is the last letter of the Hebrew alphabet, written in early Hebrew script as an X: a mark or signature, as at the end of a legal statement.
n.26: Literally "and the scroll my man of dispute has written".
n.27: Literally "I would bind it on me as crowns".
n.29: Hebrew *bo'shah*, from a verb meaning "to stink".
n.30: Job does not speak again until 40:4.

v: So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.[^1]
וַֽיִּשְׁבְּת֡וּ שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָ֭אֵלֶּה מֵעֲנ֣וֹת אֶת־אִיּ֑וֹב כִּ֤י ה֖וּא צַדִּ֣יק בְּעֵינָֽיו׃ פ
Then Elihu[^2] son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, became angry. He was angry with Job because he had justified himself rather than God.[^3]
וַיִּ֤חַר אַ֨ף ׀ אֱלִיה֣וּא בֶן־בַּרַכְאֵ֣ל הַבּוּזִי֮ מִמִּשְׁפַּ֢חַ֫ת רָ֥ם בְּ֭אִיּוֹב חָרָ֣ה אַפּ֑וֹ עַֽל־צַדְּק֥וֹ נַ֝פְשׁ֗וֹ מֵאֱלֹהִֽים׃
He was also angry with Job's three friends, because they had found no answer and yet had condemned Job.[^4]
וּבִשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת רֵעָיו֮ חָרָ֢ה אַ֫פּ֥וֹ עַ֤ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־מָצְא֣וּ מַעֲנֶ֑ה וַ֝יַּרְשִׁ֗יעוּ אֶת־אִיּֽוֹב׃
Elihu had waited to speak to Job,[^5] because they were older than he was.
וֶֽאֱלִיה֗וּ חִכָּ֣ה אֶת־אִ֭יּוֹב בִּדְבָרִ֑ים כִּ֤י זְֽקֵנִים־הֵ֖מָּה מִמֶּ֣נּוּ לְיָמִֽים׃
But when Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouths of the three men, he became angry.
וַיַּ֤רְא אֱלִיה֗וּא כִּ֘י אֵ֤ין מַעֲנֶ֗ה בְּ֭פִי שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים וַיִּ֥חַר אַפּֽוֹ׃ פ
So Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answered:[^6] "I am young in years, and you are old. That is why I held back[^7] and was afraid to tell you what I know.
וַיַּ֤עַן ׀ אֱלִיה֖וּא בֶן־בַּֽרַכְאֵ֥ל הַבּוּזִ֗י וַיֹּ֫אמַֽ[m]ר צָ֘עִ֤יר אֲנִ֣י לְ֭יָמִים וְאַתֶּ֣ם יְשִׁישׁ֑‍ִים עַל־כֵּ֖ן זָחַ֥לְתִּי וָֽאִירָ֓א ׀ מֵחַוֺּ֖ת דֵּעִ֣י אֶתְכֶֽם׃
I thought, 'Age should speak, and many years should teach wisdom.'[^8]
אָ֭מַרְתִּי יָמִ֣ים יְדַבֵּ֑רוּ וְרֹ֥ב שָׁ֝נִ֗ים יֹדִ֥יעוּ חָכְמָֽה׃
But it is the spirit in a person,[^9] the breath of the Almighty,[^10] that gives them understanding.
אָ֭כֵן רֽוּחַ־הִ֣יא בֶאֱנ֑וֹשׁ וְנִשְׁמַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י תְּבִינֵֽם׃
It is not the old[^11] who are wise, nor the aged who understand what is right.
לֹֽא־רַבִּ֥ים יֶחְכָּ֑מוּ וּ֝זְקֵנִ֗ים יָבִ֥ינוּ מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
So I say, listen to me; let me also tell you what I know.
לָכֵ֣ן אָ֭מַרְתִּי שִׁמְעָה־לִּ֑י אֲחַוֶּ֖ה דֵעִ֣י אַף־אָֽנִי׃
Look, I waited for your words; I listened to your reasoning, while you searched for what to say.
הֵ֤ן הוֹחַ֨לְתִּי לְֽדִבְרֵיכֶ֗ם אָ֭זִין עַד־תְּב֥וּנֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם עַֽד־תַּחְקְר֥וּן מִלִּֽין׃
I paid close attention to you, but not one of you refuted Job[^12] or answered his words.
וְעָֽדֵיכֶ֗ם אֶתְבּ֫וֹנָ֥ן וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֵ֣ין לְאִיּ֣וֹב מוֹכִ֑יחַ עוֹנֶ֖ה אֲמָרָ֣יו מִכֶּֽם׃
Do not say, 'We have found wisdom; let God drive him back,[^13] not a man.'
פֶּן־תֹּ֣֭אמְרוּ מָצָ֣אנוּ חָכְמָ֑ה אֵ֖ל יִדְּפֶ֣נּוּ לֹא־אִֽישׁ׃
He has not directed his words against me, and I will not answer him with your arguments.
וְלֹא־עָרַ֣ךְ אֵלַ֣י מִלִּ֑ין וּ֝בְאִמְרֵיכֶ֗ם לֹ֣א אֲשִׁיבֶֽנּוּ׃
They are dismayed; they answer no more; words have deserted them.[^14]
חַ֭תּוּ לֹא־עָ֣נוּ ע֑וֹד הֶעְתִּ֖יקוּ מֵהֶ֣ם מִלִּֽים׃
Must I wait because they do not speak, because they stand there and answer no more?
וְ֭הוֹחַלְתִּי כִּי־לֹ֣א יְדַבֵּ֑רוּ כִּ֥י עָ֝מְד֗וּ לֹא־עָ֥נוּ עֽוֹד׃
I too will give my answer;[^15] I too will tell what I know.
אַעֲנֶ֣ה אַף־אֲנִ֣י חֶלְקִ֑י אֲחַוֶּ֖ה דֵעִ֣י אַף־אָֽנִי׃
For I am full of words; the spirit within me presses me.[^16]
כִּ֭י מָלֵ֣תִי מִלִּ֑ים הֱ֝צִיקַ֗תְנִי ר֣וּחַ בִּטְנִֽי׃
Look, my belly is like wine that has no vent; like new wineskins, it is ready to burst.
הִנֵּֽה־בִטְנִ֗י כְּיַ֥יִן לֹא־יִפָּתֵ֑חַ כְּאֹב֥וֹת חֲ֝דָשִׁ֗ים יִבָּקֵֽעַ׃
Let me speak and find relief;[^17] let me open my lips and answer.
אֲדַבְּרָ֥ה וְיִֽרְוַֽח־לִ֑י אֶפְתַּ֖ח שְׂפָתַ֣י וְאֶֽעֱנֶֽה׃
I will not show partiality to anyone or flatter any person.[^18]
אַל־נָ֭א אֶשָּׂ֣א פְנֵי־אִ֑ישׁ וְאֶל־אָ֝דָ֗ם לֹ֣א אֲכַנֶּֽה׃
For I do not know how to flatter; if I did, my Maker would soon carry me away.[^19]
כִּ֤י לֹ֣א יָדַ֣עְתִּי אֲכַנֶּ֑ה כִּ֝מְעַ֗ט יִשָּׂאֵ֥נִי עֹשֵֽׂנִי׃

n.1: The Greek Septuagint reads "in their eyes".
n.2: *Elihu* means "He is my God". *Buz* was a son of Nahor, Abraham's brother (Genesis 22:21).
n.3: Literally "because he declared his soul righteous rather than God", or "before God".
n.4: An ancient Jewish scribal tradition counts this among places where the scribes changed the text out of reverence for God, from "and so had condemned God".
n.5: Literally "Elihu had waited for Job with words".
n.6: Elihu speaks from here to the end of chapter 37.
n.7: Hebrew *zachalti*, a rare verb, related to the word for creatures that crawl in the dust (Deuteronomy 32:24).
n.8: Literally "Days should speak, and many years make wisdom known".
n.9: Or "But truly it is a spirit in a mortal". Hebrew *ruach*, "spirit, breath".
n.10: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain.
n.11: Literally "the many", perhaps "the great" or "those many in years".
n.12: Literally "there was no one among you to rebuke (or convince) Job".
n.13: Literally "God will drive him away", as the wind drives away chaff.
n.14: Literally "they have moved words away from themselves". In verses 15–16, Elihu speaks about the three friends rather than to them.
n.15: Literally "my portion".
n.16: Literally "the spirit of my belly presses me". Or "the wind in my belly". Hebrew *ruach*.
n.17: Literally "that it may be roomy for me".
n.18: Literally "I will not lift up anyone's face, and to a human being (*adam*) I will not give titles".
n.19: Literally "in a little while my Maker would lift me up".

v: "But now, Job, hear what I have to say, and listen to all my words.
וְֽאוּלָ֗ם שְׁמַֽע־נָ֣א אִיּ֣וֹב מִלָּ֑י וְֽכָל־דְּבָרַ֥י הַאֲזִֽינָה׃
Look, I open my mouth; my tongue speaks in my mouth.[^1]
הִנֵּה־נָ֭א פָּתַ֣חְתִּי פִ֑י דִּבְּרָ֖ה לְשׁוֹנִ֣י בְחִכִּֽי׃
My words come from an upright heart, and my lips speak sincerely what they know.[^2]
יֹֽשֶׁר־לִבִּ֥י אֲמָרָ֑י וְדַ֥עַת שְׂ֝פָתַ֗י בָּר֥וּר מִלֵּֽלוּ׃
The spirit of God[^3] has made me; the breath of the Almighty[^4] gives me life.
רֽוּחַ־אֵ֥ל עָשָׂ֑תְנִי וְנִשְׁמַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י תְּחַיֵּֽנִי׃
Answer me if you can; set out your case before me; take your stand.
אִם־תּוּכַ֥ל הֲשִׁיבֵ֑נִי עֶרְכָ֥ה לְ֝פָנַ֗י הִתְיַצָּֽבָה׃
Look, before God I am just as you are;[^5] I too was pinched off from clay.
הֵן־אֲנִ֣י כְפִ֣יךָ לָאֵ֑ל מֵ֝חֹ֗מֶר קֹרַ֥צְתִּי גַם־אָֽנִי׃
So no fear of me need terrify you, and my pressure[^6] will not be heavy on you.
הִנֵּ֣ה אֵ֭מָתִי לֹ֣א תְבַעֲתֶ֑ךָּ וְ֝אַכְפִּ֗י עָלֶ֥יךָ לֹא־יִכְבָּֽד׃
But you have said in my hearing, and I heard the sound of your words:
אַ֭ךְ אָמַ֣רְתָּ בְאָזְנָ֑י וְק֖וֹל מִלִּ֣ין אֶשְׁמָֽע׃
'I am pure, without transgression; I am clean, and there is no guilt in me.
זַ֥ךְ אֲנִ֗י בְּֽלִ֫י פָ֥שַׁע חַ֥ף אָנֹכִ֑י וְלֹ֖א עָוֺ֣ן לִֽי׃
Look, he finds pretexts[^7] against me; he counts me as his enemy.
הֵ֣ן תְּ֭נוּאוֹת עָלַ֣י יִמְצָ֑א יַחְשְׁבֵ֖נִי לְאוֹיֵ֣ב לֽוֹ׃
He puts my feet in the stocks; he watches all my paths.'[^8]
יָשֵׂ֣ם בַּסַּ֣ד רַגְלָ֑י יִ֝שְׁמֹ֗ר כָּל־אָרְחֹתָֽי׃
Look, in this you are not right, I answer you, for God[^9] is greater than any mortal.
הֶן־זֹ֣את לֹא־צָדַ֣קְתָּ אֶעֱנֶ֑ךָּ כִּֽי־יִרְבֶּ֥ה אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַ מֵאֱנֽוֹשׁ׃
Why do you contend with him, saying that he answers none of a person's words?[^10]
מַ֭דּוּעַ אֵלָ֣יו רִיב֑וֹתָ כִּ֥י כָל־דְּ֝בָרָ֗יו לֹ֣א יַעֲנֶֽה׃
For God speaks in one way, and in two, though people do not notice it.
כִּֽי־בְאַחַ֥ת יְדַבֶּר־אֵ֑ל וּ֝בִשְׁתַּ֗יִם לֹ֣א יְשׁוּרֶֽנָּה׃
In a dream, a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on people as they slumber on their beds,
בַּחֲל֤וֹם ׀ חֶזְי֬וֹן לַ֗יְלָה בִּנְפֹ֣ל תַּ֭רְדֵּמָה עַל־אֲנָשִׁ֑ים בִּ֝תְנוּמ֗וֹת עֲלֵ֣י מִשְׁכָּֽב׃
then he opens people's ears and seals their warning,[^11]
אָ֣ז יִ֭גְלֶה אֹ֣זֶן אֲנָשִׁ֑ים וּבְמֹ֖סָרָ֣ם יַחְתֹּֽם׃
to turn a person away from what he is doing,[^12] and to keep a man from pride.[^13]
לְ֭הָסִיר אָדָ֣ם מַעֲשֶׂ֑ה וְגֵוָ֖ה מִגֶּ֣בֶר יְכַסֶּֽה׃
He keeps his soul back from the pit,[^14] his life from crossing the channel of death.[^15]
יַחְשֹׂ֣ךְ נַ֭פְשׁוֹ מִנִּי־שָׁ֑חַת וְ֝חַיָּת֗וֹ מֵעֲבֹ֥ר בַּשָּֽׁלַח׃
A person is also disciplined with pain on his bed, while all his bones are in constant torment,[^16]
וְהוּכַ֣ח בְּ֭מַכְאוֹב עַל־מִשְׁכָּב֑וֹ *וריב **וְר֖וֹב עֲצָמָ֣יו אֵתָֽן׃
so that his life loathes bread, and his soul the food it once craved.[^17]
וְזִֽהֲמַ֣תּוּ חַיָּת֣וֹ לָ֑חֶם וְ֝נַפְשׁ֗וֹ מַאֲכַ֥ל תַּאֲוָֽה׃
His flesh wastes away until it cannot be seen, and his bones, once hidden, stick out.[^18]
יִ֣כֶל בְּשָׂר֣וֹ מֵרֹ֑אִי *ושפי **וְשֻׁפּ֥וּ עַ֝צְמוֹתָ֗יו לֹ֣א רֻאּֽוּ׃
His soul draws near to the pit, and his life to those who bring death.[^19]
וַתִּקְרַ֣ב לַשַּׁ֣חַת נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וְ֝חַיָּת֗וֹ לַֽמְמִתִֽים׃
If there is an angel[^20] for him, a mediator,[^21] one among a thousand, to tell a person what is right for him,[^22]
אִם־יֵ֤שׁ עָלָ֨יו ׀ מַלְאָ֗ךְ מֵלִ֗יץ אֶחָ֥ד מִנִּי־אָ֑לֶף לְהַגִּ֖יד לְאָדָ֣ם יָשְׁרֽוֹ׃
and he is gracious to him and says, 'Spare him[^23] from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom,'
וַיְחֻנֶּ֗נּוּ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר פְּ֭דָעֵהוּ מֵרֶ֥דֶת שָׁ֗חַת מָצָ֥אתִי כֹֽפֶר׃
then his flesh becomes fresher than a child's;[^24] he returns to the days of his youth.
רֻֽטֲפַ֣שׁ בְּשָׂר֣וֹ מִנֹּ֑עַר יָ֝שׁ֗וּב לִימֵ֥י עֲלוּמָֽיו׃
He prays to God, and God accepts him; he sees his face with a shout of joy, and he restores to the mortal his righteousness.[^25]
יֶעְתַּ֤ר אֶל־אֱל֨וֹהַּ ׀ וַיִּרְצֵ֗הוּ וַיַּ֣רְא פָּ֭נָיו בִּתְרוּעָ֑ה וַיָּ֥שֶׁב לֶ֝אֱנ֗וֹשׁ צִדְקָתֽוֹ׃
He sings before people and says, 'I sinned and perverted what was right, but I was not repaid as I deserved.'[^26]
יָשֹׁ֤ר ׀ עַל־אֲנָשִׁ֗ים וַיֹּ֗אמֶר חָ֭טָאתִי וְיָשָׁ֥ר הֶעֱוֵ֗יתִי וְלֹא־שָׁ֥וָה לִֽי׃
He has redeemed his soul from going down to the pit, and his life will see the light.[^27]
פָּדָ֣ה *נפשי **נַ֭פְשׁוֹ מֵעֲבֹ֣ר בַּשָּׁ֑חַת *וחיתי **וְ֝חַיָּתוֹ בָּא֥וֹר תִּרְאֶֽה׃
Look, God does all these things, twice, three times, with a man,
הֶן־כָּל־אֵ֭לֶּה יִפְעַל־אֵ֑ל פַּעֲמַ֖יִם שָׁל֣וֹשׁ עִם־גָּֽבֶר׃
to bring back his soul from the pit, so that he may be lit with the light of life.[^28]
לְהָשִׁ֣יב נַ֭פְשׁוֹ מִנִּי־שָׁ֑חַת לֵ֝א֗וֹר בְּא֣וֹר הַֽחַיִּים׃
Pay attention, Job, listen to me; be silent, and I will speak.
הַקְשֵׁ֖ב אִיּ֥וֹב שְֽׁמַֽע־לִ֑י הַ֝חֲרֵ֗שׁ וְאָנֹכִ֥י אֲדַבֵּֽר׃
If you have anything to say, answer me; speak, for I want to prove you right.
אִם־יֵשׁ־מִלִּ֥ין הֲשִׁיבֵ֑נִי דַּ֝בֵּ֗ר כִּֽי־חָפַ֥צְתִּי צַדְּקֶֽךָּ׃
If not, listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom."
אִם־אַ֭יִן אַתָּ֥ה שְֽׁמַֽע־לִ֑י הַ֝חֲרֵ֗שׁ וַאֲאַלֶּפְךָ֥ חָכְמָֽה׃ ס

n.1: Literally "in my palate".
n.2: Literally "The uprightness of my heart is my sayings, and the knowledge of my lips they speak purely".
n.3: Or "The Spirit of God", "The breath of God". Hebrew *ruach*.
n.4: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain.
n.5: Literally "Look, I am like your mouth to God".
n.6: Hebrew *akhpi*, a word found only here, perhaps "pressure" or "hand" (compare 13:21).
n.7: Hebrew *tenu'ot*, "pretexts, occasions for hostility".
n.8: Job's own words in 13:27; compare 13:24.
n.9: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job. Also in verse 26.
n.10: Literally "for all his words he does not answer". Or "for he gives no account of any of his doings".
n.11: Literally "and he seals their discipline". The same consonants can be read "and he terrifies them with warnings".
n.12: Literally "to turn aside a human being (*adam*) from a deed".
n.13: Literally "and pride from a man he covers".
n.14: Hebrew *shachat*, the grave, the world of the dead. Also in verses 22, 24, 28 and 30.
n.15: Hebrew *shelach*, perhaps a channel or river of the underworld, or a weapon: "from perishing by the sword".
n.16: The Hebrew text is written "and the strife in his bones is constant" but read "and the multitude of his bones is constant", that is, all his bones are in constant pain.
n.17: Literally "food of desire".
n.18: The Hebrew text is written "and the bareness of his bones" but read "and his bones are laid bare". Literally "his bones that were not seen are laid bare".
n.19: Hebrew *memitim*, "those who put to death": perhaps angels of death, or the dead.
n.21: Hebrew *melits*, "interpreter, spokesman": one who speaks for another (compare 16:20; Genesis 42:23).
n.22: Literally "to declare to a human being (*adam*) his uprightness": either what is right for him to do, or that he is upright.
n.23: Hebrew *pede'ehu*, a form found only here. Some scholars read *pedehu*, "Ransom him", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.24: Hebrew *rutafash*, a word found only here, probably "grow fresh". Literally "his flesh is fresher than youth".
n.25: That is, God restores him to a right standing.
n.26: Literally "and it was not made equal to me".
n.27: The Hebrew text is written "my soul … my life" but read "his soul … his life". With the written form, the man's words continue to the end of this verse.
n.28: Literally "to be lit with the light of the living".

v: Then Elihu answered:[^1]
וַיַּ֥עַן אֱלִיה֗וּא וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"Hear my words, you wise men; listen to me, you who have knowledge.
שִׁמְע֣וּ חֲכָמִ֣ים מִלָּ֑י וְ֝יֹדְעִ֗ים הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ לִֽי׃
For the ear tests words as the palate tastes food.
כִּי־אֹ֭זֶן מִלִּ֣ין תִּבְחָ֑ן וְ֝חֵ֗ךְ יִטְעַ֥ם לֶאֱכֹֽל׃
Let us choose for ourselves what is right;[^2] let us find out among ourselves what is good.
מִשְׁפָּ֥ט נִבְחֲרָה־לָּ֑נוּ נֵדְעָ֖ה בֵינֵ֣ינוּ מַה־טּֽוֹב׃
For Job has said, 'I am in the right, and God has denied me justice.[^3]
כִּֽי־אָ֭מַר אִיּ֣וֹב צָדַ֑קְתִּי וְ֝אֵ֗ל הֵסִ֥יר מִשְׁפָּטִֽי׃
In spite of my right, I am counted a liar;[^4] my wound[^5] is incurable, though I am without transgression.'
עַל־מִשְׁפָּטִ֥י אֲכַזֵּ֑ב אָנ֖וּשׁ חִצִּ֣י בְלִי־פָֽשַׁע׃
What man is like Job, who drinks up scorn like water,
מִי־גֶ֥בֶר כְּאִיּ֑וֹב יִֽשְׁתֶּה־לַּ֥עַג כַּמָּֽיִם׃
who keeps company with evildoers, and walks with wicked men?
וְאָרַ֣ח לְ֭חֶבְרָה עִם־פֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָ֑וֶן וְ֝לָלֶ֗כֶת עִם־אַנְשֵׁי־רֶֽשַׁע׃
For he has said, 'It does a man no good to be on good terms with God.'[^6]
כִּֽי־אָ֭מַר לֹ֣א יִסְכָּן־גָּ֑בֶר בִּ֝רְצֹת֗וֹ עִם־אֱלֹהִֽים׃
So listen to me, you men of understanding.[^7] Far be it from God to do wickedness, and from the Almighty[^8] to do wrong!
לָכֵ֤ן ׀ אַֽ[m]נֲשֵׁ֥י לֵבָ֗ב שִׁמְע֫וּ לִ֥י חָלִ֖לָה לָאֵ֥ל מֵרֶ֗שַׁע וְשַׁדַּ֥י מֵעָֽוֶל׃
For he repays a person for what he has done, and he brings on each one what his conduct deserves.[^9]
כִּ֤י פֹ֣עַל אָ֭דָם יְשַׁלֶּם־ל֑וֹ וּֽכְאֹ֥רַח אִ֝֗ישׁ יַמְצִאֶֽנּוּ׃
Truly, God will not act wickedly, and the Almighty will not pervert justice.
אַף־אָמְנָ֗ם אֵ֥ל לֹֽא־יַרְשִׁ֑יעַ וְ֝שַׁדַּ֗י לֹֽא־יְעַוֵּ֥ת מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
Who put him in charge of the earth? Who set the whole world in place?
מִֽי־פָקַ֣ד עָלָ֣יו אָ֑רְצָה וּמִ֥י שָׂ֝֗ם תֵּבֵ֥ל כֻּלָּֽהּ׃
If he were to set his heart on himself,[^10] and gather to himself his spirit and his breath,[^11]
אִם־יָשִׂ֣ים אֵלָ֣יו לִבּ֑וֹ רוּח֥וֹ וְ֝נִשְׁמָת֗וֹ אֵלָ֥יו יֶאֱסֹֽף׃
all flesh would perish together, and humankind would return to dust.
יִגְוַ֣ע כָּל־בָּשָׂ֣ר יָ֑חַד וְ֝אָדָ֗ם עַל־עָפָ֥ר יָשֽׁוּב׃
If you have understanding, hear this; listen to what I say.[^12]
וְאִם־בִּ֥ינָה שִׁמְעָה־זֹּ֑את הַ֝אֲזִ֗ינָה לְק֣וֹל מִלָּֽי׃
Can one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the one who is righteous and mighty?
הַאַ֬ף שׂוֹנֵ֣א מִשְׁפָּ֣ט יַחֲב֑וֹשׁ וְאִם־צַדִּ֖יק כַּבִּ֣יר תַּרְשִֽׁיעַ׃
Is it fitting to say to a king, 'Worthless one,'[^13] or to nobles, 'Wicked'?
הַאֲמֹ֣ר לְמֶ֣לֶךְ בְּלִיָּ֑עַל רָ֝שָׁ֗ע אֶל־נְדִיבִֽים׃
He shows no partiality to princes and does not favor the rich over the poor, for they are all the work of his hands.
אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־נָשָׂ֨א ׀ פְּנֵ֥י שָׂרִ֗ים וְלֹ֣א נִּ[t]כַּר־שׁ֭וֹעַ לִפְנֵי־דָ֑ל כִּֽי־מַעֲשֵׂ֖ה יָדָ֣יו כֻּלָּֽם׃
In a moment they die; at midnight people are shaken and pass away; the mighty are removed without a hand.[^14]
רֶ֤גַע ׀ יָמֻתוּ֮ וַחֲצ֢וֹת לָֽ[m]יְלָה יְגֹעֲשׁ֣וּ עָ֣ם וְיַעֲבֹ֑רוּ וְיָסִ֥ירוּ אַ֝בִּ֗יר לֹ֣א בְיָֽד׃
For his eyes are on a person's ways, and he sees all his steps.
כִּי־עֵ֭ינָיו עַל־דַּרְכֵי־אִ֑ישׁ וְֽכָל־צְעָדָ֥יו יִרְאֶֽה׃
There is no darkness, no deep darkness,[^15] where evildoers can hide.
אֵֽין־חֹ֭שֶׁךְ וְאֵ֣ין צַלְמָ֑וֶת לְהִסָּ֥תֶר שָׁ֝֗ם פֹּ֣עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃
For he does not need to consider a person further[^16] before he comes before God in judgment.
כִּ֤י לֹ֣א עַל־אִ֭ישׁ יָשִׂ֣ים ע֑וֹד לַהֲלֹ֥ךְ אֶל־אֵ֝֗ל בַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃
He shatters the mighty without investigation[^17] and sets others in their place.
יָרֹ֣עַ כַּבִּירִ֣ים לֹא־חֵ֑קֶר וַיַּעֲמֵ֖ד אֲחֵרִ֣ים תַּחְתָּֽם׃
Because he knows their deeds, he overthrows them in the night, and they are crushed.
לָכֵ֗ן יַ֭כִּיר מַעְבָּֽדֵיהֶ֑ם וְהָ֥פַךְ לַ֝֗יְלָה וְיִדַּכָּֽאוּ׃
He strikes them for their wickedness[^18] where others can see,
תַּֽחַת־רְשָׁעִ֥ים סְפָקָ֗ם בִּמְק֥וֹם רֹאִֽים׃
because they turned aside from following him and paid no attention to any of his ways,
אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־כֵּ֭ן סָ֣רוּ מֵֽאַחֲרָ֑יו וְכָל־דְּ֝רָכָ֗יו לֹ֣א הִשְׂכִּֽילוּ׃
so that they brought the cry of the poor before him, and he hears the cry of the afflicted.
לְהָבִ֣יא עָ֭לָיו צַֽעֲקַת־דָּ֑ל וְצַעֲקַ֖ת עֲנִיִּ֣ים יִשְׁמָֽע׃
But if he keeps quiet, who can condemn him? If he hides his face, who can see him? Yet he watches over nation and individual alike,[^19]
וְה֤וּא יַשְׁקִ֨ט ׀ וּמִ֥י יַרְשִׁ֗עַ וְיַסְתֵּ֣ר פָּ֭נִים וּמִ֣י יְשׁוּרֶ֑נּוּ וְעַל־גּ֖וֹי וְעַל־אָדָ֣ם יָֽחַד׃
so that the godless may not reign, and may not be snares for the people.[^20]
מִ֭מְּלֹךְ אָדָ֥ם חָנֵ֗ף מִמֹּ֥קְשֵׁי עָֽם׃
For has anyone said to God, 'I have borne punishment; I will not offend again.[^21]
כִּֽי־אֶל־אֵ֭ל הֶאָמַ֥ר נָשָׂ֗אתִי לֹ֣א אֶחְבֹּֽל׃
Teach me what I cannot see; if I have done wrong, I will do it no more'?
בִּלְעֲדֵ֣י אֶ֭חֱזֶה אַתָּ֣ה הֹרֵ֑נִי אִֽם־עָ֥וֶל פָּ֝עַ֗לְתִּי לֹ֣א אֹסִֽיף׃
Should he repay on your terms, when you have rejected his ways?[^22] For you must choose, not I; so tell us what you know.
הַֽמֵעִמְּךָ֬ יְשַׁלְמֶ֨נָּה כִּֽי־מָאַ֗סְתָּ כִּי־אַתָּ֣ה תִבְחַ֣ר וְלֹא־אָ֑נִי וּֽמַה־יָדַ֥עְתָּ דַבֵּֽר׃
Men of understanding will say to me, and any wise man who hears me:
אַנְשֵׁ֣י לֵ֭בָב יֹ֣אמְרוּ לִ֑י וְגֶ֥בֶר חָ֝כָ֗ם שֹׁמֵ֥עַֽ לִֽי׃
'Job speaks without knowledge; his words are without insight.'
אִ֭יּוֹב לֹא־בְדַ֣עַת יְדַבֵּ֑ר וּ֝דְבָרָ֗יו לֹ֣א בְהַשְׂכֵּֽיל׃
If only Job were tested to the end[^23] for answering like wicked men!
אָבִ֗י יִבָּחֵ֣ן אִיּ֣וֹב עַד־נֶ֑צַח עַל־תְּ֝שֻׁבֹ֗ת בְּאַנְשֵׁי־אָֽוֶן׃
For he adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us[^24] and multiplies his words against God."
כִּ֥י יֹ֘סִ֤יף עַֽל־חַטָּאת֣וֹ פֶ֭שַׁע בֵּינֵ֣ינוּ יִסְפּ֑וֹק וְיֶ֖רֶב אֲמָרָ֣יו לָאֵֽל׃ ס

n.1: Literally "And Elihu answered and said". No one has spoken since 33:33: the formula marks a new part of Elihu's speech, as in 35:1 and 36:1.
n.2: Hebrew *mishpat*: justice, what is right.
n.3: Job's words in 27:2; compare 13:18.
n.4: Literally "Concerning my right I lie". Or "Should I lie about my right?"
n.5: Literally "my arrow" (compare 6:4).
n.6: Literally "when he delights himself with God". Compare 9:22; 21:15.
n.7: Literally "men of heart". Also in verse 34.
n.8: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain. Also in verse 12.
n.9: Literally "according to a man's path he makes it find him".
n.10: Literally "If he sets his heart toward himself", that is, if he thought only of himself. Or "If he set his mind to it".
n.11: Hebrew *ruach* and *neshamah*, the breath of life that God gives (Genesis 2:7; Psalm 104:29).
n.12: Here *you* is singular: Elihu speaks to Job.
n.13: Hebrew *beliyya'al*, "worthless, good-for-nothing".
n.14: That is, without human help: by God's power.
n.15: Hebrew *tsalmavet*, "deep darkness", traditionally read as "the shadow of death".
n.16: Literally "For he does not set upon a man further". Some scholars read *mo'ed*, "an appointed time", for *od*, "further", with a small change to the Hebrew: "he does not set a time for anyone".
n.17: Literally "without searching".
n.18: Literally "In place of the wicked he slaps them": either "as wicked people" or "for their wickedness".
n.19: Literally "both over a nation and over a human being (*adam*) together".
n.20: The Hebrew of verses 29–33 is very difficult, and the translation is uncertain in places. Literally "from the reigning of a godless man, from snares of a people".
n.21: Literally "I have borne; I will not act corruptly".
n.22: Literally "Is it from with you that he will repay it, for you have rejected?"
n.23: Hebrew *avi*, usually "my father". Here it is perhaps an expression of wish, "If only".

v: Then Elihu answered:[^1]
וַיַּ֥עַן אֱלִיה֗וּ וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"Do you think this is just? You say, 'I am more in the right than God.'[^2]
הֲ֭זֹאת חָשַׁ֣בְתָּ לְמִשְׁפָּ֑ט אָ֝מַ֗רְתָּ צִדְקִ֥י מֵאֵֽל׃
For you ask, 'What use is it to you?[^3] What do I gain by not sinning?'[^4]
כִּֽי־תֹ֭אמַר מַה־יִּסְכָּן־לָ֑ךְ מָֽה־אֹ֝עִ֗יל מֵֽחַטָּאתִֽי׃
I will answer you, and your friends with you.
אֲ֭נִי אֲשִֽׁיבְךָ֣ מִלִּ֑ין וְֽאֶת־רֵעֶ֥יךָ עִמָּֽךְ׃
Look up at the heavens and see; gaze at the clouds, high above you.
הַבֵּ֣ט שָׁמַ֣יִם וּרְאֵ֑ה וְשׁ֥וּר שְׁ֝חָקִ֗ים גָּבְה֥וּ מִמֶּֽךָּ׃
If you have sinned, what do you do to him? If your transgressions are many, what do you do to him?
אִם־חָ֭טָאתָ מַה־תִּפְעָל־בּ֑וֹ וְרַבּ֥וּ פְ֝שָׁעֶ֗יךָ מַה־תַּעֲשֶׂה־לּֽוֹ׃
If you are righteous, what do you give him? Or what does he receive from your hand?
אִם־צָ֭דַקְתָּ מַה־תִּתֶּן־ל֑וֹ א֥וֹ מַה־מִיָּדְךָ֥ יִקָּֽח׃
Your wickedness affects only someone like yourself, and your righteousness only a human being.[^5]
לְאִישׁ־כָּמ֥וֹךָ רִשְׁעֶ֑ךָ וּלְבֶן־אָ֝דָ֗ם צִדְקָתֶֽךָ׃
Because of the many oppressions,[^6] people cry out; they cry for help because of the arm of the mighty.
מֵ֭רֹב עֲשׁוּקִ֣ים יַזְעִ֑יקוּ יְשַׁוְּע֖וּ מִזְּר֣וֹעַ רַבִּֽים׃
But no one says, 'Where is God[^7] my Maker, who gives songs in the night,
וְֽלֹא־אָמַ֗ר אַ֭יֵּה אֱל֣וֹהַּ עֹשָׂ֑י נֹתֵ֖ן זְמִר֣וֹת בַּלָּֽיְלָה׃
who teaches us more than the animals of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?'[^8]
מַ֭לְּפֵנוּ מִבַּהֲמ֣וֹת אָ֑רֶץ וּמֵע֖וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם יְחַכְּמֵֽנוּ׃
There they cry out, but he does not answer, because of the pride of evildoers.
שָׁ֣ם יִ֭צְעֲקוּ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲנֶ֑ה מִ֝פְּנֵ֗י גְּא֣וֹן רָעִֽים׃
Surely God does not listen to an empty cry;[^9] the Almighty[^10] pays no attention to it.
אַךְ־שָׁ֭וְא לֹא־יִשְׁמַ֥ע ׀ אֵ֑ל וְ֝שַׁדַּ֗י לֹ֣א יְשׁוּרֶֽנָּה׃
How much less when you say that you do not see him, that your case is before him, and you are waiting for him!
אַ֣ף כִּֽי־תֹ֭אמַר לֹ֣א תְשׁוּרֶ֑נּוּ דִּ֥ין לְ֝פָנָ֗יו וּתְח֥וֹלֵֽל לֽוֹ׃
And now, because his anger does not punish, and he does not take much notice of transgression,[^11]
וְעַתָּ֗ה כִּי־אַ֭יִן פָּקַ֣ד אַפּ֑וֹ וְלֹֽא־יָדַ֖ע בַּפַּ֣שׁ מְאֹֽד׃
Job opens his mouth in empty talk;[^12] he multiplies words without knowledge."
וְ֭אִיּוֹב הֶ֣בֶל יִפְצֶה־פִּ֑יהוּ בִּבְלִי־דַ֝֗עַת מִלִּ֥ין יַכְבִּֽר׃ פ

n.1: Literally "And Elihu answered and said" (see 34:1).
n.2: Literally "my righteousness from God": either "my righteousness is more than God's" or "I am in the right before God".
n.3: Either Job speaking to God, or Elihu repeating Job's question in his own words: "What use is it to you, Job?"
n.4: Literally "What do I gain more than from my sin?"
n.5: Literally "a son of *adam*", that is, of humankind.
n.6: Or "the many oppressors".
n.7: Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job.
n.8: Or "who teaches us by the animals of the earth, and makes us wise by the birds of the sky" (compare 12:7).
n.9: Literally "Surely emptiness God does not hear".
n.10: Hebrew *Shaddai*, traditionally "the Almighty"; the meaning is uncertain.
n.11: Hebrew *pash*, a word found only here, perhaps "arrogance" or "folly". It may be a form of *pesha*, "transgression".
n.12: Hebrew *hevel*, "breath, vapor": what has no substance.

v: Elihu continued:[^1]
וַיֹּ֥סֶף אֱלִיה֗וּא וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
"Bear with me a little longer, and I will show you, for there is still more to say on God's behalf.[^2]
כַּתַּר־לִ֣י זְ֭עֵיר וַאֲחַוֶּ֑ךָּ כִּ֤י ע֖וֹד לֶאֱל֣וֹהַּ מִלִּֽים׃
I will bring my knowledge from far away, and I will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
אֶשָּׂ֣א דֵ֭עִי לְמֵרָח֑וֹק וּ֝לְפֹעֲלִ֗י אֶֽתֵּֽן־צֶֽדֶק׃
For truly my words are not false; one who is perfect in knowledge[^3] is with you.
כִּֽי־אָ֭מְנָם לֹא־שֶׁ֣קֶר מִלָּ֑י תְּמִ֖ים דֵּע֣וֹת עִמָּֽךְ׃
Look, God is mighty, and he does not despise anyone; he is mighty in strength of understanding.[^4]
הֶן־אֵ֣ל כַּ֭בִּיר וְלֹ֣א יִמְאָ֑ס כַּ֝בִּ֗יר כֹּ֣חַֽ לֵֽב׃
He does not keep the wicked alive, but he gives justice to the afflicted.
לֹא־יְחַיֶּ֥ה רָשָׁ֑ע וּמִשְׁפַּ֖ט עֲנִיִּ֣ים יִתֵּֽן׃
He does not take his eyes off the righteous; he seats them with kings on the throne forever, and they are exalted.
לֹֽא־יִגְרַ֥ע מִצַּדִּ֗יק עֵ֫ינָ֥יו וְאֶת־מְלָכִ֥ים לַכִּסֵּ֑א וַיֹּשִׁיבֵ֥ם לָ֝נֶ֗צַח וַיִּגְבָּֽהוּ׃
But if they are bound in chains, caught in the cords of affliction,
וְאִם־אֲסוּרִ֥ים בַּזִּקִּ֑ים יִ֝לָּכְד֗וּן בְּחַבְלֵי־עֹֽנִי׃
then he tells them what they have done, and their transgressions, that they have behaved arrogantly.
וַיַּגֵּ֣ד לָהֶ֣ם פָּעֳלָ֑ם וּ֝פִשְׁעֵיהֶ֗ם כִּ֣י יִתְגַּבָּֽרוּ׃
He opens their ears to instruction[^5] and tells them to turn back from wickedness.
וַיִּ֣גֶל אָ֭זְנָם לַמּוּסָ֑ר וַ֝יֹּ֗אמֶר כִּֽי־יְשֻׁב֥וּן מֵאָֽוֶן׃
If they listen and serve him, they will end their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasantness.
אִֽם־יִשְׁמְע֗וּ וְֽיַעֲ֫בֹ֥דוּ יְכַלּ֣וּ יְמֵיהֶ֣ם בַּטּ֑וֹב וּ֝שְׁנֵיהֶ֗ם בַּנְּעִימִֽים׃
But if they do not listen, they will cross the channel of death[^6] and die without knowledge.
וְאִם־לֹ֣א יִ֭שְׁמְעוּ בְּשֶׁ֣לַח יַעֲבֹ֑רוּ וְ֝יִגְוְע֗וּ כִּבְלִי־דָֽעַת׃
The godless in heart harbor anger;[^7] they do not cry for help when he binds them.
וְֽחַנְפֵי־לֵ֭ב יָשִׂ֣ימוּ אָ֑ף לֹ֥א יְ֝שַׁוְּע֗וּ כִּ֣י אֲסָרָֽם׃
They die in their youth, and their life ends among the shrine prostitutes.[^8]
תָּמֹ֣ת בַּנֹּ֣עַר נַפְשָׁ֑ם וְ֝חַיָּתָ֗ם בַּקְּדֵשִֽׁים׃
He rescues the afflicted through their affliction and opens their ears through their distress.
יְחַלֵּ֣ץ עָנִ֣י בְעָנְי֑וֹ וְיִ֖גֶל בַּלַּ֣חַץ אָזְנָֽם׃
He also lured you[^9] out of the jaws of distress, into a broad place where there was no constraint,[^10] and your table was set with rich food.[^11]
וְאַ֤ף הֲסִיתְךָ֨ ׀ מִפִּי־צָ֗ר רַ֭חַב לֹא־מוּצָ֣ק תַּחְתֶּ֑יהָ וְנַ֥חַת שֻׁ֝לְחָנְךָ֗ מָ֣לֵא דָֽשֶׁן׃
But you are full of the judgment due to the wicked; judgment and justice take hold of you.
וְדִין־רָשָׁ֥ע מָלֵ֑אתָ דִּ֖ין וּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט יִתְמֹֽכוּ׃
Beware that wrath[^12] does not lure you into scoffing,[^13] and do not let a large ransom[^14] turn you aside.
כִּֽי־חֵ֭מָה פֶּן־יְסִֽיתְךָ֣ בְסָ֑פֶק וְרָב־כֹּ֝֗פֶר אַל־יַטֶּֽךָּ׃
Will your cry for help keep you out of distress, or all the efforts of your strength?[^15]
הֲיַעֲרֹ֣ךְ שׁ֭וּעֲךָ לֹ֣א בְצָ֑ר וְ֝כֹ֗ל מַאֲמַצֵּי־כֹֽחַ׃
Do not long for the night, when peoples are taken away from their place.[^16]
אַל־תִּשְׁאַ֥ף הַלָּ֑יְלָה לַעֲל֖וֹת עַמִּ֣ים תַּחְתָּֽם׃
Be careful not to turn to wickedness, for you have chosen this rather than affliction.[^17]
הִ֭שָּׁמֶר אַל־תֵּ֣פֶן אֶל־אָ֑וֶן כִּֽי־עַל־זֶ֝֗ה בָּחַ֥רְתָּ מֵעֹֽנִי׃
Look, God is exalted in his power. Who is a teacher like him?
הֶן־אֵ֭ל יַשְׂגִּ֣יב בְּכֹח֑וֹ מִ֖י כָמֹ֣הוּ מוֹרֶֽה׃
Who has prescribed his way for him? Who can say, 'You have done wrong'?
מִֽי־פָקַ֣ד עָלָ֣יו דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וּמִֽי־אָ֝מַ֗ר פָּעַ֥לְתָּ עַוְלָֽה׃
Remember to extol his work, which people have praised in song.
זְ֭כֹר כִּֽי־תַשְׂגִּ֣יא פָעֳל֑וֹ אֲשֶׁ֖ר שֹׁרְר֣וּ אֲנָשִֽׁים׃
All humankind has looked on it; mortals see it from afar.
כָּל־אָדָ֥ם חָֽזוּ־ב֑וֹ אֱ֝נ֗וֹשׁ יַבִּ֥יט מֵרָחֽוֹק׃
Look, God is great, beyond our knowledge; the number of his years is past searching out.
הֶן־אֵ֣ל שַׂ֭גִּיא וְלֹ֣א נֵדָ֑ע מִסְפַּ֖ר שָׁנָ֣יו וְלֹא־חֵֽקֶר׃
For he draws up the drops of water; they distill rain from his mist,[^18]
כִּ֭י יְגָרַ֣ע נִטְפֵי־מָ֑יִם יָזֹ֖קּוּ מָטָ֣ר לְאֵדֽוֹ׃
which the skies pour down and shower on humankind in abundance.
אֲשֶֽׁר־יִזְּל֥וּ שְׁחָקִ֑ים יִ֝רְעֲפ֗וּ עֲלֵ֤י ׀ אָדָ֬ם רָֽב׃
Can anyone understand the spreading of the clouds, the thundering from his pavilion?[^19]
אַ֣ף אִם־יָ֭בִין מִפְרְשֵׂי־עָ֑ב תְּ֝שֻׁא֗וֹת סֻכָּֽ[t]תֽוֹ׃
Look, he spreads his light around him, and he covers the roots of the sea.[^20]
הֵן־פָּרַ֣שׂ עָלָ֣יו אוֹר֑וֹ וְשָׁרְשֵׁ֖י הַיָּ֣ם כִּסָּֽה׃
For by these he judges[^21] the peoples; he gives food in abundance.
כִּי־בָ֭ם יָדִ֣ין עַמִּ֑ים יִֽתֶּן־אֹ֥כֶל לְמַכְבִּֽיר׃
He covers his hands with lightning[^22] and commands it to strike the mark.
עַל־כַּפַּ֥יִם כִּסָּה־א֑וֹר וַיְצַ֖ו עָלֶ֣יהָ בְמַפְגִּֽיעַ׃
His thunder announces him;[^23] even the cattle tell of the storm's approach.[^24]
יַגִּ֣יד עָלָ֣יו רֵע֑וֹ מִ֝קְנֶ֗ה אַ֣ף עַל־עוֹלֶֽה׃

n.1: Literally "And Elihu added and said".
n.2: Literally "for there are still words for God". Hebrew *Eloah*, a poetic form of *Elohim*, "God", used often in Job.
n.3: Elihu speaks of himself. The same phrase is used of God in 37:16.
n.4: Literally "mighty in strength of heart". The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain.
n.5: Or "discipline". Hebrew *musar*.
n.6: Hebrew *shelach*, as in 33:18. Or "they will perish by the sword".
n.7: Literally "set anger".
n.8: Hebrew *qedeshim*, men attached to shrines, probably as cult prostitutes (Deuteronomy 23:18 (23:17 in most English Bibles)). Their lives end early and in shame.
n.9: Or "He is luring you". The Hebrew of verses 16–20 is very difficult, and the translation is uncertain in places.
n.10: Literally "breadth, not constraint beneath it".
n.11: Literally "and the setting of your table was full of fatness".
n.12: Or "heat", "anger". Literally "For wrath, lest it lure you".
n.13: Hebrew *safeq*, "clapping", a gesture of scorn (34:37), or "abundance".
n.14: Or "a large bribe". Hebrew *kofer*, as in 33:24.
n.15: The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain. Or "Will your wealth be valued, not in gold, nor all the resources of your strength?"
n.16: Literally "to go up, peoples, beneath them".
n.17: Some scholars read *bochanta*, "you have been tested", for *bacharta*, "you have chosen", with a small change to the Hebrew: "for because of this you have been tested by affliction".
n.18: Hebrew *ed*, a rare word also found in Genesis 2:6.
n.19: Hebrew *sukkah*, "shelter, booth": the clouds around God (Psalm 18:12 (18:11 in most English Bibles)).
n.20: That is, the depths of the sea.
n.23: The Hebrew of this verse is very uncertain. Literally "His noise tells about him".
n.24: Literally "the cattle, even concerning what goes up". Some scholars read "he is jealous with anger against wrongdoing", with a small change to the Hebrew.

v: "At this my heart also trembles and leaps from its place.
אַף־לְ֭זֹאת יֶחֱרַ֣ד לִבִּ֑י וְ֝יִתַּ֗ר מִמְּקוֹמֽוֹ׃
Listen, listen to the roar of his voice,[^1] the rumbling that comes from his mouth.
שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמ֣וֹעַ בְּרֹ֣גֶז קֹל֑וֹ וְ֝הֶ֗גֶה מִפִּ֥יו יֵצֵֽא׃
He lets it loose under the whole heaven, and his lightning[^2] to the ends of the earth.
תַּֽחַת־כָּל־הַשָּׁמַ֥יִם יִשְׁרֵ֑הוּ וְ֝אוֹר֗וֹ עַל־כַּנְפ֥וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
After it his voice roars; he thunders with his majestic voice, and he does not hold back the lightning[^3] when his voice is heard.
אַחֲרָ֤יו ׀ יִשְׁאַג־ק֗וֹל יַ֭רְעֵם בְּק֣וֹל גְּאוֹנ֑וֹ וְלֹ֥א יְ֝עַקְּבֵ֗ם כִּֽי־יִשָּׁמַ֥ע קוֹלֽוֹ׃
God thunders wonderfully with his voice; he does great things that we cannot understand.
יַרְעֵ֤ם אֵ֣ל בְּ֭קוֹלוֹ נִפְלָא֑וֹת עֹשֶׂ֥ה גְ֝דֹל֗וֹת וְלֹ֣א נֵדָֽע׃
For he says to the snow, 'Fall on the earth,' and to the rain shower, his mighty downpours.[^4]
כִּ֤י לַשֶּׁ֨לַג ׀ יֹאמַ֗ר הֱוֵ֫א אָ֥רֶץ וְגֶ֥שֶׁם מָטָ֑ר וְ֝גֶ֗שֶׁם מִטְר֥וֹת עֻזּֽוֹ׃
He seals up the hand of every person,[^5] so that all the people he has made may know it.[^6]
בְּיַד־כָּל־אָדָ֥ם יַחְתּ֑וֹם לָ֝דַ֗עַת כָּל־אַנְשֵׁ֥י מַעֲשֵֽׂהוּ׃
The animals go into their dens and stay in their lairs.
וַתָּבֹ֣א חַיָּ֣ה בְמוֹ־אָ֑רֶב וּבִמְע֖וֹנֹתֶ֣יהָ תִשְׁכֹּֽן׃
The storm comes out from its chamber,[^7] and the cold from the scattering winds.[^8]
מִן־הַ֭חֶדֶר תָּב֣וֹא סוּפָ֑ה וּֽמִמְּזָרִ֥ים קָרָֽה׃
By the breath of God ice is given, and the broad waters are frozen solid.[^9]
מִנִּשְׁמַת־אֵ֥ל יִתֶּן־קָ֑רַח וְרֹ֖חַב מַ֣יִם בְּמוּצָֽק׃
He loads the thick cloud with moisture;[^10] the clouds scatter his lightning.[^11]
אַף־בְּ֭רִי יַטְרִ֣יחַ עָ֑ב יָ֝פִ֗יץ עֲנַ֣ן אוֹרֽוֹ׃
They turn round and round by his guidance,[^12] to do all that he commands them over the face of the inhabited earth.
וְה֤וּא מְסִבּ֨וֹת ׀ מִתְהַפֵּ֣ךְ *בתחבולתו **בְּתַחְבּוּלֹתָ֣יו לְפָעֳלָ֑ם כֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְצַוֵּ֓ם ׀ עַל־פְּנֵ֖י תֵבֵ֣ל אָֽרְצָה׃
Whether for punishment,[^13] or for his land, or for faithful love,[^14] he makes it happen.
אִם־לְשֵׁ֥בֶט אִם־לְאַרְצ֑וֹ אִם־לְ֝חֶ֗סֶד יַמְצִאֵֽהוּ׃
Listen to this, Job; stop and consider the wonders of God.
הַאֲזִ֣ינָה זֹּ֣את אִיּ֑וֹב עֲ֝מֹ֗ד וְהִתְבּוֹנֵ֤ן ׀ נִפְלְא֬וֹת אֵֽל׃
Do you know how God[^15] directs them[^16] and makes the lightning of his cloud shine?
הֲ֭תֵדַע בְּשׂוּם־אֱל֣וֹהַּ עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְ֝הוֹפִ֗יעַ א֣וֹר עֲנָנֽוֹ׃
Do you know how the clouds are balanced,[^17] the wonders of one who is perfect in knowledge?[^18]
הֲ֭תֵדַע עַל־מִפְלְשֵׂי־עָ֑ב מִ֝פְלְא֗וֹת תְּמִ֣ים דֵּעִֽים׃
You, whose clothes are hot when the land lies still under the south wind,
אֲשֶׁר־בְּגָדֶ֥יךָ חַמִּ֑ים בְּהַשְׁקִ֥ט אֶ֝֗רֶץ מִדָּרֽוֹם׃
can you, as he does, spread out the skies, hard as a mirror of cast metal?[^19]
תַּרְקִ֣יעַ עִ֭מּוֹ לִשְׁחָקִ֑ים חֲ֝זָקִ֗ים כִּרְאִ֥י מוּצָֽק׃
Teach us what we should say to him; we cannot set out our case because of the darkness.
ה֭וֹדִיעֵנוּ מַה־נֹּ֣אמַר ל֑וֹ לֹֽ[m]א נַ֝עֲרֹ֗ךְ מִפְּנֵי־חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
Should he be told that I want to speak? Would anyone ask to be swallowed up?[^20]
הֽ͏ַיְסֻפַּר־ל֖[d]וֹ כִּ֣י אֲדַבֵּ֑ר אִֽם־אָ֥מַר אִ֝֗ישׁ כִּ֣י יְבֻלָּֽע׃
Now no one can look at the light when it is bright in the skies, when the wind has passed and swept them clean.[^21]
וְעַתָּ֤ה ׀ לֹ֘א רָ֤אוּ א֗וֹר בָּהִ֣יר ה֭וּא בַּשְּׁחָקִ֑ים וְר֥וּחַ עָ֝בְרָ֗ה וַֽתְּטַהֲרֵֽם׃
Out of the north comes golden splendor;[^22] around God is awesome majesty.
מִ֭צָּפוֹן זָהָ֣ב יֶֽאֱתֶ֑ה עַל־אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַּ נ֣וֹרָא הֽוֹד׃
The Almighty:[^23] we cannot find him. He is great in power, and in justice and abundant righteousness he does not oppress.
שַׁדַּ֣י לֹֽא־מְ֭צָאנֻהוּ שַׂגִּיא־כֹ֑חַ וּמִשְׁפָּ֥ט וְרֹב־צְ֝דָקָ֗ה לֹ֣א יְעַנֶּֽה׃
Therefore people fear him; he does not regard any who are wise in their own heart."[^24]
לָ֭כֵן יְרֵא֣וּהוּ אֲנָשִׁ֑ים לֹֽא־יִ֝רְאֶ֗ה כָּל־חַכְמֵי־לֵֽב׃ פ

n.1: Or "his thunder". Hebrew *qol*, "voice", is also the word for thunder. Also in verses 4 and 5.
n.2: Literally "his light". Also in verses 11 and 15.
n.3: Literally "them", probably the lightning bolts of verse 3.
n.4: Literally "and the shower of rain, and the shower of the rains of his strength".
n.5: That is, he stops all human work during the storms of winter. Literally "In the hand of every human being (*adam*) he seals".
n.6: Literally "to know, all the men of his work".
n.7: Literally "from the chamber", perhaps "the chambers of the south" (9:9).
